articles.title: Earps, Putellas and how London City can afford their high-profile transfers
articles.summary: The names just kept coming, one after the other: Alexia Putellas, a two-time Ballon d’Or winner; Mary Earps, named the best women’s goalkeeper by FIFA in 202...
articles.body:
The names just kept coming, one after the other: Alexia Putellas, a two-time Ballon d'Or winner; Mary Earps, named the best women's goalkeeper by FIFA in 2022 and 2023; Mapi Leon, a four-time Champions League winner; and Kadidiatou Diani, who has earned more than 100 caps for France.

But how are the London City Lionesses, owned by American businesswoman Michele Kang, complying with the Women's Super League's financial rules to pay these big-name players?

Kang, a Korean-American businesswoman, bought the club in 2023 , helping them win promotion to the WSL in 2025. Finishing sixth in their debut top-flight season was respectable, but this summer, they have gone big. London City have splashed out on star players — albeit mostly on free transfers — for two reasons: they want to qualify for the Champions League and increase their revenue as soon as possible.

Earnings have to rise so they can afford to pay this set of players. London City are banking on marquee names attracting larger sponsorship deals and a new fanbase that will increase revenue down the line. On Thursday they announced a first-of-its-kind multi-year front-of-shirt partnership with Nike. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. Kang, however, said the value exceeds some Premier League men's teams' shirt deals and the $4million (£2.9 m) annual value of the NWSL's Atlanta expansion franchise's recent front-of-shirt agreement, believed to be the wealthiest jersey sponsorship in women's sports.

Invest before revenue is a common strategy in women's football and reflects its 'start-up' nature . In a league where attendances have stalled , London City have taken it upon themselves, for better or worse, to inject some dynamism into the WSL.

"That piece of the puzzle (revenue) is missing," Christina Philippou, associate professor in sport finance at the University of Portsmouth, tells The Athletic . "But Kang is too smart for this to be: 'Let's go wild and spend for fun'." As Kang has proven in the past , if she wants to make something happen, she will.

The WSL introduced financial rules a year ago but crucially, any breach of the salary cost could not be enforced until this upcoming season.

The WSL's permitted squad salary requirement (PSS) limits clubs to spending a proportion of revenue on players, but allows for increased spending when owners provide equity funding.

PSS limits spending on player salaries to 80 per cent of a club's annual revenues, plus an allowance for 'relevant cash funding', capped at 25 per cent of those annual revenues or £4million ($5.4m), whichever is higher.

"That allows for some owner investment to push the team forward but not go completely wild," says Philippou.

Relevant cash funding from owners doesn't have to be equity, with 'soft loans' — interest-free borrowings that are at the back of the queue when it comes to the team's liabilities — also included. For most clubs, such funding will max out at £4m. At last check (accounts for the 2024-25 financial year), only Chelsea and Arsenal recorded revenues beyond £16m, suggesting only they could inject more than £4m.

Determining a WSL team's relevant revenues will require more nuance than has previously been evident. PSS dictates clubs can't count money sent from fellow group undertakings (ie, men's teams) as revenue, and any revenue from sponsorship deals spanning both forms must be 'reasonably allocated'. That will require a clear definition of splits to be distributed between the men's and women's teams going forward.

Whatever the topline figure ends up being, clubs will only be able to spend 80 per cent of it on their 'total salary cost' — a slightly misleading tagline, as it only refers to players' wages. The WSL has laid out a list of what comprises these player salary costs, including player agent payments and image rights.

Notable exceptions include pension contributions, payments towards player education, parental leave or childcare, helping ensure that clubs don't cut back under the guise of compliance with the rules.

How much have London City spent and what are the risks?

Well, we won't know until the financial accounts are released in approximately 18 months. But according to multiple sources — speaking anonymously to protect relationships, like some others in this piece — there is no player at London City earning a baseline salary of more than £1million.

London City have been criticised for inflating wages at the top end of the market, but one source points to Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw's salary — Manchester City's star striker signed a new four-year contract in June that, as The Athletic reported, is worth an annual £1.6m , excluding performance-related bonuses. There is an argument, however, that London City's activity has driven wages at the middle-to-lower levels of the table, where clubs are fighting to build their fanbases and compete.

Over the coming years, London City plan to shift their sights to younger, more affordable players, keep wages down, and hope the allure of their squad, facilities, and the prospect of competing in Europe will attract the next generation of talent. They do not want to become the go-to team for out-of-contract 32-year-olds.

During their promotion 2024-25 season from the Championship (now WSL 2), their total expenditure (£11.5m) was the fourth-highest in English women's football, only behind Arsenal (£21.6m), Chelsea (£20.2m) and Manchester City (£14.0m). Their revenue was only £902,000, in contrast to Chelsea (£21.3m), Arsenal (£21.5m), Manchester United (£10.7m) and City (£10.6m). Generating revenue is vital now that London City have higher-earning players on their books.

The independent club has, according to a source with knowledge of the matter, developed a five-year business plan to make the project sustainable and profitable. Any club can spend now but their revenue generated at the end of the season, when they have to declare their figures, is an estimate. London City's fanbase, according to the source, has already significantly increased and sponsors are offering more because of the names attached to the club. The WSL also negotiated an improved five-year TV deal , starting from the 2025-26 season, which will increase revenue.

The risk is overestimating the impact of such transfers, especially in the case of their biggest star, Putellas. What if sponsorship deals do not come off? What if she gets injured or wants to move? What if the new fans at their ground in Bromley, south London, with a capacity of just 5,160, are not engaged as the club predicted? There are a lot of what-ifs, but London City are hedging their bets.

What are the punishments if a club breaches the PSS?

Let's be clear: there is no sense that London City have done anything wrong yet.

Perhaps learning from the past ambiguity of sanctions in the Premier League , the WSL has been prescriptive when detailing what might befall London City, or anyone, if they breach PSS.

The regulations section breaches are split into four types: minor procedural, major procedural, salary floor threshold and salary cost threshold.

The former two range in seriousness from late filings to 'attempts to circumvent' the rules in bad faith by, for example, "falsifying exclusions to redirect funds to a player and therefore reduce their salary cap value". Minor procedural breaches carry low penalties but major ones can lead to point deductions.

A salary floor threshold breach occurs when clubs are found to have paid players less than the bare minimum required by WSL rules. Those salary floors are flexed by age and tier: in the top flight, minimum salaries range from £26,900 for players aged 18-20 to £42,500 for over-23s; in WSL2, the range is £17,500 to £26,900. A breach here sees clubs allowed time to rectify the issue. If they don't, point deductions are possible.

Salary cost threshold breaches — which, from the outside, look like London City's most obvious concern — are split into their own minor and major categories.

A minor breach is when a club exceeds its threshold by up to 20 per cent and incurs a fine. They taper upwards in line with the size of the breach and can total up to 40 per cent of the club's excess spending. For example, if the maximum amount a club can spend, according to revenue generated, is £10m but they spend 20 per cent more (£12m) they will be fined 40 per cent of the £2m excess (which is £800,000).

Anything beyond a 20 per cent excess comprises a major breach and would incur a more severe fine (50 per cent of the excess) and a points deduction. If a top-flight club exceeds its salary cap by 20 per cent but by less than £100,000, they will be docked one point. Anything that is both 20 per cent and £900,000 over a club's threshold will see them docked at least 10 points. So if a club's threshold is £10m, they exceed it by 30 per cent, rising to £13m, they will be fined £1.5m and docked at least 10 points.

If clubs have not met their revenue target at the end of the season, some may embark on creative ways, such as club tours, to close the revenue gap.

Some teams in men's football could calculate that taking the financial hit and points deduction would leave them better off if they qualify for European competitions — the source, who has been briefed on the situation, stresses that is not London City's intention.

But it is still a possibility for any club.

On the one hand, bringing high-profile players into the WSL attracts more eyeballs, driving the league's growth. On the other hand, you can understand why some teams, especially mid-table clubs, may be irked. Aggressive spending widens the competitive gap between teams and creates pressure for others to invest in order to compete, potentially beyond a club's means. The financial regulations are in place to prevent clubs from doing that.

"The better your accountants and lawyers, the more wiggle room you can get," says Philippou. New regulations have lots of loopholes in them and clubs test the limits. As the league progresses, the rules get stronger and more loopholes are closed.

What is beneficial for the women's game is, when the financial accounts are published, a more transparent understanding of wage to revenue ratio. For now, London City are prepared to speculate to accumulate.

articles.title: Illinois takes down UAB in the season opener
articles.summary: Illinois moves to 1-0 on the young season.
articles.body:
Champaign, Ill — Four seconds remaining in the first half, and 54 yards away from the UAB goal line. That was the position Katin Houser was in, up only one point, on the Blazers – however, magic was about to happen.

Houser, with all the time in the world, stepped up in the pocket and fired a missile that was tipped into the hands of Ty Robinson for a touchdown, as the clock read triple zeros.

The play put Illinois (1-0) up eight heading into the half and ultimately led to their victory over the visiting UAB Blazers (0-1) by a score of 42-23.

It wasn't all sunshine and rainbows for Illinois, though. UAB gave the Illini a serious run for their money – literally. The Blazers' run game was on point in Thursday's contest, with Braylon McReynolds and Roderic Robinson II combining for 114 of the team's 194 rushing yards.

UAB also dominated the time of possession, controlling the ball for 41:03 compared to the Illini's 18:57.

To be fair, the time differential was mainly due to the Orange and Blue's success on breakaway plays.

The first one came directly after the conclusion of UAB's first drive.

Mac Resetich stood within the Illini's 10-yard line awaiting the Blazers' punt. The senior DB had just played the whole first series on defense – however, you wouldn't have been able to tell on the return. Mac took the punt 65 yards, which set up an Illini touchdown two plays later.

The touchdown would come via a Katin Houser pass to Collin Dixon, the first of two touchdowns the pair would have together.

Houser, in only his second play as an Illini, pump-faked to Brayden Trimble like it was a screen, with both Blazer DB's biting hard on it. Thus, allowing Dixon to prance into the end zone unguarded.

If we're talking big plays, though, I'd have to mention Ca'lil Valentine.

The junior running back followed up a 17-yard run with a 51-yard house call that showcased his full speed.

Valentine is up a full 20 pounds from when he arrived on campus in 2024, yet he has the same twitchiness that made him such an exciting prospect. I'd expect him to get more and more carries as the season progresses.

The game will undoubtedly be a relief for some aspects of Illinois' team. For one, Katin Houser looked eerily similar to Luke Altmyer, and the Illini DB's balled out, only allowing 219 passing yards.

However, the defense was on the field for a very long time, and if it wasn't for some undisciplined UAB penalties, today could have been a lot more costly.

However, for the first game of the Bobby Hauck and the 3-3-5 era, I gotta give credit where credit is due. The Orange and Blue, time and time again, would stop the Blazers while they were deep in their own territory. UAB had to settle the whole game, and I think it showed the mental fortitude that this Illinois team has.

One of the craziest football plays I've ever seen in person.

Valentine will be a major piece of this offense.

The cherry on top — Ismael Kante takes this interception to the house.

Katin Houser (ILL) — 13/17, 182 Passing Yards, 3 Passing TDs, 1 Rushing TD

Collin Dixon (ILL) — 70 Receiving Yards, 6 Receptions, 2 TDs

Roderic Robinson II (UAB) — 73 Total Yards, 1 Receiving TD

Ryder Burton (UAB) – 18/32, 219 Yards, 1 TD, 1 INT

The Illini are 1-0, and things are looking more exciting than ever.

The Duke Blue Devils will come to Champaign next Saturday, looking to seek revenge after Illinois beat them handily last season in Durham.

articles.title: Y la afición del Betis se quedó sin ver goles
articles.standfirst: La primera visita del Madrid a la casa verdiblanca fue el primer empate a cero después de 52 partidos entre Liga y Copa
articles.summary: La primera visita del Madrid a la casa verdiblanca fue el primer empate a cero después de 52 partidos entre Liga y Copa
articles.body: El Betis se estrenó en Primera en la temporada 1932-33. Su campo estaba en lo que se llamaba La Huerta del Fraile y llevaba el nombre de Estadio del Patronato Obrero. Allí acudió el Madrid por primera vez para jugar un partido de Liga el 19 de febrero de 1933. Era la jornada número 13; por delante quedaban cinco más. Los verdiblancos respiraron después de cinco derrotas seguidas al sumar un punto en campo de la Real Sociedad (2-2); el Madrid caminaba de forma firme hacia su segunda Liga consecutiva, con una racha de seis jornadas en las que encadenó otras tantas victorias. Esa tarde se vio algo sin precedentes en el campo del Betis en partidos de competición nacional, tanto de Liga como de Copa: un partido en el que el encargado del marcador no tuvo labor alguna. El Betis sumaba ante su gente 19 partidos de Copa (debutó en ella el domingo 28 de febrero de 1926, ganando 3-0 al Cartagena), 27 en Segunda y los seis de esa temporada en Primera. En todos y cada uno de ellos los goles habían aparecido. Alguno solo para el equipo rival. En Segunda, Espanyol y Sevilla habían vencido en la casa del Betis dejando a los locales a cero. Fue la visita del campeón de Liga en vigor, y que también lo sería unas semanas después, la que inauguró el historial de partidos a cero con el Betis como local. Era el partido número 53 en el Patronato entre duelos de Liga y de Copa. Era la lengua nativa de los entrenadores de los dos equipos. A los mandos del Betis estaba el irlandés Patrick Joseph O’Connell, afincado en España desde su llegada a Santander en 1922 y que en 1935 dio al Betis su única Liga. El entrenador del Madrid era el inglés Robert Edwin Firth. Al igual que su colega irlandés, su llegada al fútbol español fue por la puerta de Cantabria y del Racing. En las horas previas al choque se hablaba de un partido de alto nivel. En la prensa madrileña se ponderaba la fuerza del Betis, más cuando jugaba en casa y había respirado para salvarse en la jornada previa. Pero se veía a un Madrid poderoso, lanzado. “Precisamente por lo que tiene de difícil el match con el Betis permite colocar al Madrid en situación de vencedor. Porque a los madridistas les sucede lo contrario que al hombre de la copla: que en las cuestas arriba es cuando menos precisan del burro...”, se leía en el semanal Crónica como previa del partido en Heliópolis Lo que era entusiasmo cuando el catalán dio el pitido para arrancar el partido, se tornó en decepción. Los dos equipos anduvieron espesos, con un juego aburrido, deslabazado y plomizo. Todo lo que se esperaba de las figuras del líder quedó en casi nada. Sólo en el tramo final, apremiados por el 0-0, los dos equipo aceleraron en busca del gol. No llegó. En el Betis, el mejor fue Timimi. En la pocas ocasiones que superó al dúo Ciriaco-Quincoces se chocó con los reflejos de Zamora. En el Madrid fueron Samitier y Luis Regueiro quienes más acosaron al meta bético, el vizcaíno Joaquín Urquiaga. El canario Hilario tuvo una de esas tardes en las que su genió se apagaba y parecía un fantasma sobre el verde. Mientras en Sevilla se daba por bueno el aburrido punto porque seguir en Primera para el Betis estaba cada vez más cerca, en Madrid no se dejó pasar la ocasión de apretar las tuercas al entrenador a pesar de la firme marcha del equipo. A la cabeza, el periódico El Liberal y un artículo sin firma: “La lesión de Leoncito ha obligado a Mr. Firth a tomar decisiones graves si se tiene en cuenta lo apaciblemente que se desliza la vida de un entrenador de football. Como ni usa hongo ni fuma en pipa, Mr. Firth no ha tenido más remedio que calarse el borsalino y seguir las misteriosas espirales que describe el humo de un mísero pitillo de setenta. Después, siguiendo el impulso noble que casi todo inglés experimenta ante un buen frasco de oloroso licor, se ha sacudido equis copas y se ha dado a pensar, igual que cualquiera de nuestros más exquisitos filósofos. Pero no torturemos más a míster Firth. No tenemos derecho a ello. Sería cruel eso de obligar a este hombre ejemplar a que piense tantas cosas seguidas. Yes”. Tinta con veneno.

articles.title: Arsenal sell Martinelli to Al-Hilal in post-transfer deadline day deal
articles.summary: Brazil forward Gabriel Martinelli transfers to Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal from Premier League champions Arsenal.
articles.body:
Arsenal forward Gabriel Martinelli has joined Saudi side Al-Hilal, the Premier League champions have announced.

No fee was disclosed but British media reports said the deal, finalised late on Thursday, was worth a guaranteed 60 million pounds ($81m).

That would make 25-year-old Brazil international Martinelli the most expensive player to leave the London club, following Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain’s 35 million pounds ($47m) exit to Liverpool in 2017.

Martinelli has signed a four-year deal with Al-Hilal, who are currently joint-top of the Saudi Pro League with Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr.

“Gabriel Martinelli has joined Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal on a permanent transfer,” said a statement on Arsenal’s website.

“Proud to be blue, proud to be Al-Hilal,” said Martinelli during an unveiling video on his new club’s social media channels.

He will join Ollie Watkins at Al-Hilal after the England striker left Aston Villa in a deal worth an estimated 51 million pounds ($69m).

Martinelli’s departure comes after Arsenal sold fellow left-sided forward Leandro Trossard to Besiktas.

Christos Tzolis has joined from Club Brugge, but there are concerns that the exits of Martinelli and Trossard could leave Arsenal short of personnel in that part of the pitch.

Martinelli made 53 appearances in all competitions last season, scoring 11 goals, as the Gunners won the top-flight title for the first time since 2004.

His nearly 300 games for Arsenal, including 62 goals, also saw him involved in their 2020 FA Cup and 2023 Community Shield successes.

He was left out of Arsenal’s first two matchday squads of the season, however, with manager Mikel Arteta making it clear Martinelli would struggle for game time were he to remain at the Emirates Stadium.

Former Arsenal striker Ian Wright criticised the club’s decision to omit Martinelli from the squad for the opening game against Coventry.

“The way Martinelli is being treated at the moment, it really makes me feel uncomfortable,” Wright told Sky Sports.

“I know they might want him out, and a lot of people might say, ‘yeah, it’s time for him to move him on’. But there’s ways of doing that, and it should suit him as well, how he wants to leave.”

The closure of the European transfer window on Tuesday only prevents clubs within the continent from buying players, but not from selling them.

articles.title: Riquelme: "Durante un tiempo largo, quizá excesivo, dejé de disfrutar"
articles.standfirst: El futbolista madrileño del Betis se sincera en MARCA antes de enfrentarse al Real Madrid
articles.summary: El futbolista madrileño del Betis se sincera en MARCA antes de enfrentarse al Real Madrid
articles.body: Rodrigo Riquelme (Madrid, 2 de abril de 2000) atraviesa su mejor momento desde que llegó al Betis. Tras una temporada de adaptación, en la que las cosas no le terminaron de salir como esperaba, el exjugador del Atlético de Madrid logró cambiar el chip gracias a una charla con Manuel Pellegrini, uno de sus grandes valedores, y vuelve a disfrutar del fútbol. Suma dos goles en las tres primeras jornadas y esta noche apunta a titular frente al Real Madrid, el eterno rival de su exequipo y al que ya marcó un gol que nunca olvidará en una eliminatoria de Copa. Antes del partido, se sincera en MARCA y habla de la importancia de la salud mental en el deporte de élite. Pregunta. Después de un resultado como el del sábado, ¿cómo se encuentra el vestuario? ¿Han tenido tiempo de analizar qué ocurrió? Respuesta. Empezamos después del partido del sábado, ese 5-2, a analizar un poco qué es lo que pasó. Como siempre se está después de una derrota más abultada, el míster ha sido claro que hay que pensar ya en el siguiente partido, que corregiremos errores y que tenemos que trabajar un partido que es muy bonito y que tenemos muchas ganas de jugarlo con nuestra gente, perdón. P. Llamaron especialmente la atención los problemas defensivos y en las acciones a balón parado. ¿Han detectado qué falló? R. Es cierto que llevamos una buena dinámica en pretemporada, en la que no hemos concedido muchos goles. Luego, al inicio de Liga, los dos primeros partidos tampoco hemos concedido goles, pero es fútbol. Son acciones en las que hay que estar al 2000% concentrados. Fueron puntuales y es cierto que pudimos hacer más, pudimos incluso ponernos por delante, pero es fútbol y, como te he dicho, corregir errores y seguir. P. Venían de dos victorias consecutivas y de un inicio muy bueno. ¿Pudo haber algo de exceso de confianza? R. No creo que seamos un equipo en el que nos confiemos o que bajemos los brazos. Creo que hay partidos que salen de una manera y que salen de otra, pero no creo que la palabra sea que nos hayamos confiado. P. En lo personal ha empezado muy bien, titular y marcando goles. ¿Esperaba arrancar así la temporada? R. Al final esto es como un poco el resultado de todo un trabajo que yo he hecho a nivel mental y físico. Terminé la temporada pasada muy bien, con muy buenas sensaciones. Estuve entrenando dos veces al día durante todas las vacaciones. Volví mejor haciendo muchísimo trabajo mental, mucho hincapié en eso, y volví bien. Creo que hice una buena pretemporada que me ayudó a coger confianza, a ver todo un poquito más claro. Como te he dicho, es un poco el resultado de todo esto, pero es simplemente el comienzo de la Liga. A nivel personal he empezado bien, pero me centro y pongo el foco en cómo terminé, cómo volví y en cómo estoy, que es en el día a día, que es lo que a mí me hace fuerte y no me obsesiono ni pienso más allá del hoy. Pregunta. En apenas tres partidos ha superado ya su registro goleador de toda la Liga pasada. ¿Se ha quitado un peso de encima? Respuesta. No te digo un peso encima, igual es un poco adaptarme también a todo. Cada persona y cada jugador tiene su periodo de adaptación. Yo el año pasado lo tuve, lo pasé y, como te he dicho antes, con mucho trabajo, mucha dedicación, mucho trabajo mental, ahora mismo me siento muy bien. P. Ha contado que este verano ha perdido grasa y ganado músculo. ¿Qué trabajo específico ha realizado? ¿Ha cambiado también alimentación o hábitos? R. Está claro. Yo soy un chico siempre con muy buenos hábitos, con la alimentación siempre muy cuidada porque creo que eso es fundamental, y más hoy en día. He seguido un poquito con la misma idea en cuanto a descanso, pautas, tiempos de relajación, alimentación, insisto, muy bien. De hecho, volví en pretemporada con menos grasa, con 2 kilos más de masa muscular. Entonces es un trabajo en el que le he hecho mucho hincapié, no solo a nivel físico, insisto, también muchísimo, diría que incluso más a nivel mental, que me está ayudando a sentirme bien, a recuperar mejor, a intentar ponerle las cosas difíciles al entrenador y a demostrar que estoy aquí por algo. P. ¿Qué buscaba con ese cambio físico? ¿Sentirse más potente, más explosivo, resistir mejor el cuerpo a cuerpo con los defensas? R. Al final el músculo no pesa, lo que pesa es la grasa. Para encontrarme yo mejor, al final cuando uno se siente bien físicamente a nivel corporal, se atreve más a hacer cosas y es algo que a mí me ayuda mucho. P. También ha hablado de un cambio mental. Usted ha dicho alguna vez que si no disfruta no puede rendir. ¿Riquelme está volviendo a disfrutar del fútbol? R. Absolutamente, absolutamente. Además te agradezco que me hagas esta pregunta porque es una cosa que durante un tiempo largo, quizás excesivo, dejé de disfrutar, dejé de otra vez sentir ese niño pequeño cuando sale al campo. Además, jugadores de mi perfil, de mi forma de jugar, si no nos divertimos, realmente no explotamos todas nuestras condiciones. Como te he dicho antes, creo que ese trabajo mental que he hecho, el relativizar ciertas cosas o el poner el foco en las cosas que realmente merecen la pena y que a mí me sirven, me han ayudado otra vez a disfrutar. La verdad que sí. P. ¿Cómo se entrena la cabeza de un futbolista para recuperar esa confianza? R. Yo trabajo, llevo trabajando con una persona desde los 18 años te diría, que es una persona genial. Me ha ayudado en cualquier ámbito de mi vida y sigo a día de hoy trabajando con la misma persona. Mucha parte de esto creo que también es gracias a esa ayuda, aparte de por supuesto mi entorno, mi pareja, mi familia, mis amigos. Pero un poquito más entrando en detalle a lo profesional, está siempre que yo lo necesito, tanto si van bien las cosas como si van mal. Creo que es importante mantener esa estabilidad y si le puede servir a muchos jugadores o muchos chicos jóvenes que están empezando hoy, que nos estén escuchando, yo les animo a que lo hagan porque van a notar una diferencia muy grande. Pregunta. Si tuviera que resumirlo, ¿qué hace hoy Riquelme que no hacía hace un año? Respuesta. Creo que estoy, como te he dicho antes, entrenando mucho más. A la hora de la alimentación todo bien, sigo manteniendo esos hábitos porque yo siempre he tenido muy buenos hábitos. Darle mucha importancia al descanso, al sueño, a la forma de recuperar, al tema de estar en contacto con la naturaleza, con los fisios, con todo. A mí eso me hace recuperar y me hace sentir mucho mejor. P. ¿Siente que ésta es una temporada fundamental para consolidarse definitivamente como un jugador importante en el Betis? R. Mira, si te soy sincero, no me pongo a pensar en eso porque creo que ahora mismo no toca. Está claro que todos necesitamos nuestro periodo de adaptación, como te he dicho antes. Confío mucho en mí, confío mucho en mis capacidades, en todo lo que estoy trabajando y si es este año, pues mira, genial, perfecto. Yo aseguro que lo estoy haciendo todo para que así sea y para volver a disfrutar del fútbol. No me pongo piedras en la mochila, ni presión, ni expectativas, ni nada. P. Pellegrini ha sido uno de sus grandes valedores. ¿Cómo es su relación y qué importancia tuvo su confianza durante los momentos difíciles? R. Bien, bien. El míster es una persona con mucho conocimiento, ya no solo de fútbol sino de la vida. Ha estado en grandísimos clubes, los más grandes del mundo prácticamente. Es muy conocedor de todo: vestuario, personalidades. Yo el año pasado tuve una conversación con él que a mí me ayudó, me hizo cambiar el chip un poco, en donde él creía que yo tenía que mejorar, poner el foco. Desde que me puse a ello, me siento bien, siento que le estoy respondiendo y eso para un jugador, el saber que estás haciendo lo que el míster te pide, es vital. P. ¿Qué le está pidiendo ahora sobre el campo? ¿Más presencia ofensiva, más llegada al área, más gol? R. Sí, sí. Al final los jugadores de ataque tenemos que acercarnos al gol, tenemos que tratar de generar peligro, por supuesto, y de materializar las ocasiones que genere el equipo, y por supuesto también ayudar defensivamente. Pero sí, está claro que es una faceta que el míster pide, no solamente a mí, sino a todos los jugadores de ataque y es una cosa que, como hemos hablado antes, he empezado con buen pie. P. Se enfrentan a una temporada exigente con el reto de la Champions. En el vestuario hay campeones del torneo y muchos jugadores que han disputado la competición, como es su caso. ¿Cree que esa experiencia puede ayudar al Betis? R. Sí, sí, al final nosotros lo que tenemos es mucha ambición, tenemos mucha ilusión, muchas ganas de volver a vivir noches así. Hemos jugado muchos de la plantilla partidos de Champions, partidos importantes de Champions, y creo que eso nos va a ayudar como equipo a que nos sintamos más cómodos en la competición. Pregunta. El sorteo ha sido complicado. ¿Dónde cree que puede estar la clave para superar la Fase de Liga? Respuesta. Estar juntos, dar el 100% en cada acción, cada minuto, cada jugada y, evidentemente, los partidos en casa con nuestra gente van a ser fundamentales. P. Pero antes de pensar en la Champions llega el Real Madrid... R. Ahora mismo estamos centrados en la Liga, que empezamos bien, hemos tenido ahí un tropezón, cosas de fútbol, y ahora tenemos un partido muy bonito que queremos darle una alegría al aficionado bético y en eso estamos ahora mismo con el foco puesto. P. Para un madrileño criado desde niño en el Atlético, ¿enfrentarse al Real Madrid continúa siendo un partido especial aunque ahora vista de verdiblanco? R. Sí, está claro que sí. Además, ellos han empezado muy bien, están en un nivel muy alto, cambiaron al entrenador, han traído muy buenos jugadores y, como te he dicho, va a ser un partido muy difícil como siempre es, pero bonito de jugar. P. Ya sabe lo que es marcarle al Real Madrid, con aquel gol en el 119' para cerrar el 4-2 de Copa en el Metropolitano. ¿Es uno de los goles más especiales de su carrera? R. Sí, probablemente el que más ilusión te hace marcar, ya no solo por contra quién lo marcas, sino cómo fue la eliminatoria en el Metropolitano y todo. Además, yo que soy canterano del Atlético de Madrid, fue como un subidón bastante grande para mí. P. ¿Cómo está viendo al Madrid desde el regreso de Mourinho? ¿En qué cree que ha cambiado? R. Está claro que tener un entrenador de nivel máximo... Es cierto que tampoco consumo mucho fútbol, pero por lo que he podido ver, se le ve un equipo más consolidado, más hecho, con las ideas más claras. Pregunta. Mbappé y Bellingham han empezado a un nivel altísimo a la vuelta del Mundial. ¿Impone encontrarse a futbolistas así en este momento de forma? Respuesta. Está claro, estamos hablando de dos de los probablemente diez mejores jugadores del mundo, cien por cien, si no es en los cinco seguro. Con nuestras armas trataremos de complicarles el partido, de hacer que no se sientan cómodos y luego aprovechar nosotros nuestras oportunidades. P. Para preparar el partido tiene además un vestuario lleno de exmadridistas: Isco, Fran García, Fidalgo, Diego Llorente, Dani Ceballos... ¿Lo viven de una manera especial? R. Bien, de manera tranquila. Ya son gente adulta, esas cosas ya no creo que les provoquen mucha excitación por el partido, pero está claro que jugar contra el Madrid siempre hace ilusión, siempre te llena de energía, de ganas y ojalá que podamos hacer un gran encuentro. P. Hablando de exmadridistas, ¿cómo está viendo a Isco? Fue uno de los jugadores que más pendiente estuvo de usted cuando llegó al Betis. ¿Cómo ha vivido todo el proceso de su lesión? R. Si te soy sincero, le veo muy bien. De hecho, el otro día lo hablé con él, le veía muy bien, mucho más suelto, con muchísimo más ritmo, más fluido todo. Yo no voy a descubrir ahora a Isco, es un jugador como la copa de un pino y creo que tenemos que aprender mucho de él, de esa resiliencia que está teniendo en su recuperación. Insisto, le veo bien, cada vez está mejor, él incluso tiene otra cara más feliz, más alegre y, personalmente, me alegro como si fuese yo mismo. Todo el equipo creo que tenemos que arroparle, darle ese cariño y no tengo ningún tipo de duda de que va a volver a ser Isco. P. Con Fran García tiene conexión desde hace tiempo y ahora comparten banda. ¿Cómo se están entendiendo? ¿Cree que un lateral tan profundo como él puede beneficiarle a usted personalmente por su juego? R. Sí, creo que sin ningún tipo de duda. Fran como persona es una auténtica maravilla y luego como jugador también es una máquina, tiene una capacidad física brutal. Creo que la pretemporada nos ha servido mucho para entendernos, para poder combinar bien y creo que, la verdad, estamos entendiéndonos muy bien, haciendo mucho peligro por esa banda y ojalá que podamos seguir con esa buena conexión. P. A Fran le tocó enfrentarse incluso antes de llegar a la élite, en los derbis madrileños de filiales. Unos partidos en los que usted compartía equipo con Diego Conde. ¿Cómo ha sido volver a encontrarse? R. He hablado con él de su lesión, eso es mala suerte. Al final es el fútbol y esas cosas pasan. Con Diego es un chico al que siempre he tenido muchísimo cariño por cómo es a nivel personal. Él jugó con mi hermano en el Atlético de Madrid también, luego jugó conmigo en el filial, conocemos a la familia, es un chico increíble y desearle que le vaya genial y que tenga una temporada como se merece. Pregunta. Compite con Abde, pero son dos extremos muy diferentes. ¿Cree que Pellegrini tiene en ustedes dos soluciones distintas e incluso complementarias? ¿Cómo es su relación con él? Respuesta. Mi relación con él es genial, es perfecta, siempre la he tenido. Es un muy buen chico, un chico que tiene unas condiciones espectaculares. Tuvo muy mala suerte con el tema de la lesión porque venía de un año increíble y justo tocó el Mundial, cosas del fútbol. Creo que ya está recuperado, si no es al 100% es al 99%. Me alegro de corazón que esté bien porque nos va a ayudar muchísimo. Está claro que igual tenemos condiciones diferentes, pero creo que también podemos incluso llegar a jugar juntos en algún momento o lo que sea, siempre y cuando el míster lo considere, y por supuesto que está claro que es una competencia bonita y sana. P. Y han llegado nuevos jugadores en ataque. ¿Cómo está viendo a los fichajes y, en particular, a Troy Parrott? ¿Le beneficia jugar con un delantero más posicional como él? R. Facu (Bernal) creo que ha caído de pie. Desde el primer momento se le veían unas condiciones muy buenas, un muy buen chico, un chico tranquilo. Troy es cierto que lleva una semana aquí, creo que no lleva más, pero ya se le ve bien, cada vez más suelto, cada vez con más confianza. Creo que el otro día hizo un gran partido, tuvo mala suerte que el gol que metió fue fuera de juego, además que yo le di la asistencia, y creo que hizo un buen partido que nos va a ayudar una barbaridad. Creo que han sido dos fichajes que son aciertos. P. Cuando llegó dijo que sus compañeros le habían advertido de que aquí iba a descubrir “un derbi de verdad”, no como el Madrid-Atlético. Ahora que ya ha vivido los dos, ¿tenían razón? ¿Cuál es mejor? R. Creo que por el sentimiento, sobre todo también, es más por la gente cómo lo vive aquí. Sevilla no es una ciudad tan grande como Madrid y aquí está claro que o eres del Sevilla o eres del Betis, se vive de una manera increíble. A mí me sorprendió gratamente, pero está claro que allí en el Atleti los derbis también se viven a corazón abierto. Son muy similares, pero aquí es cierto que igual se vive con más pasión. P. Y para terminar, ¿ese sentimiento y la calidad humana que ha encontrado en el Betis le han ayudado también en su adaptación? R. Absolutamente. Creo que a mí lo que más me llamó la atención aquí es la calidad humana que hay, desde el que está más arriba al que está más abajo, y todos remamos en la misma dirección. Es un club que está hecho para ser así, porque la gente lo siente así, los que estamos aquí lo sentimos así, y todo esto a mí me ayuda una barbaridad a aclimatarme mejor, a sentirme valorado, al sentirme querido y tratar de devolver un poco todo eso a cualquier persona que lo necesite.

articles.title: Martín Presa: "Si nos retiran la concesión, buscaríamos construir un nuevo estadio en Vallecas, pero si es imposible, antes sobreviviríamos"
articles.standfirst: El presidente del Rayo explica la situación del estadio de Vallecas en 'El Partidazo de COPE'
articles.summary: El presidente del Rayo explica la situación del estadio de Vallecas en 'El Partidazo de COPE'.
articles.body: "Mientras yo sea presidente, si la salud me lo permite, y espero serlo muchos años más, lo último que quisiéramos es que el Rayo se fuera de Vallecas, entendiendo distrito de Vallecas, lo he dicho por activa, por pasiva, eso que quede clarísimo. Queremos seguir en Vallecas. Si a nosotros, en una hipótesis, algún día se nos retira esa concesión, tendríamos que buscar construir inmediatamente otro estadio, intentaríamos en el distrito de Vallecas, pero si eso se nos hace imposible, antes sobreviviríamos, pero es lo último que queremos", comentó Raúl Martín Presa en 'El Partidazo de COPE', donde analizó, según su punto de vista, todo lo que está ocurriendo con el estadio de Vallecas, donde, por ahora, el equipo sigue sin poder jugar. El Rayo Vallecano, de hecho, anunció este jueves a través de un comunicado que el partido ante el Racing de Santander, que se disputa este sábado a las 18.30 horas, se jugará, como ya ocurriera frente al Alavés, en el campo de Butarque. "Estábamos convencidos al 100% de que íbamos a jugar el partido del sábado en Vallecas. No comprendemos que el encuentro no se pueda jugar en Vallecas", dijo. Si la situación se repite, es decir, si el Rayo continúa sin poder jugar en Vallecas el próximo encuentro en casa contra el Espanyol, el presidente anuncia que tomarán medidas: "Visto lo visto, nosotros lo que tendremos que iniciar son medidas judiciales y pedir auxilio judicial ante este atropello que estamos sufriendo. Si las cosas están bien, para mí no es admisible lo de 'es que tiene que firmar una auditoría'". "El estadio ahora mismo está en una situación óptima", continuó Martín Presa en 'El Partidazo de COPE'. Y añadió: "La gente no corre peligro viniendo a Vallecas. El campo ha estado en condiciones correctas de mantenimiento y de seguridad. Todos los años se han hecho los simulacros de evacuación". Martín Presa también se refirió en 'El Partidazo de COPE' a las consecuencias que toda esta situación está provocando en el club y en la afición. "El daño que se hace a 15.000 personas teniendo que ir a Leganés es terrible. El daño potencial que se hace a un club como el Rayo yendo a Butarque... Estoy convencido de que los dos puntos que perdemos ante el Alavés, en Vallecas no se pierden. El riesgo deportivo al que le están sometiendo con un posible descenso, la ansiedad a los jugadores... No estamos valorando los riesgos deportivos, económicos, reputacionales y que nos están afectando hasta a la seguridad de algunas personas que trabajamos aquí".

articles.title: Una primera portería a cero agridulce
articles.standfirst: La Real no encajó un gol después de 19 partidos seguidos sin lograrlo, en muchos de ellos recibiendo dos, pero no pudo marcar para haber logrado la victoria
articles.summary: La Real no encajó un gol después de 19 partidos seguidos sin lograrlo, en muchos de ellos recibiendo dos, pero no pudo marcar para haber logrado la victoria
articles.body: La Real Sociedad logró contra el Celta mantener su portería a cero después de 19 partidos seguidos encajando gol, en la mayoría de ellos dos o tres, por lo que no recibir uno fue una buena noticia, pero el hecho de no marcar ninguno y no haber podido ganar la dejó en un segundo plano. De hecho, hasta el propio Pellegrino Matarazzo confesó al final del encuentro que hubiese preferido vencer 4-3 y haber sumado los tres puntos. Mejorar a nivel defensivo y no recibir un tanto en contra era uno de los principales objetivos de la Real para esta temporada, después de que en la pasada no lo consiguiese en las nueve jornadas finales y sólo lo lograse en tres de las 38 de LaLiga, su peor marca en mucho tiempo, terminando además como el equipo más goleado. Por si fuera poco, en la pretemporada el conjunto txuriurdin no logró solucionar ese problema atrás, al recibir una diana en los siete encuentros amistosos que realizó, en seis de ellos dos o más goles, algo que también le sucedió en hasta nueve ocasiones en la segunda parte del curso, en el que lo pagó no finalizando en posiciones europeas en LaLiga, como era su objetivo. La Real comenzó esta nueva campaña perdiendo 1-0 en La Cartuja ante el Betis y 4-1 ante el Real Madrid en el Santiago Bernabéu, para ganar luego al Espanyol, pero concediendo un tanto, 2-1, pese a que permitió muy pocas ocasiones claras del rival, como ayer frente al Celta, cuando consiguió por fin una portería a cero tras 19 partidos sin lograrla. Es evidente que el reto de los de Matarazzo es continuar con esa mejoría defensiva, pero sin perder el gran juego de ataque que han demostrado tener, para repetir pronto un encuentro sin encajar, pero en esta ocasión haciendo algún gol para ganar. El Elche, el lunes en su Martínez Valero, es el primer rival ante el que lo intentarán.

articles.summary: El futuro europeo, en juego
articles.body: La sede de la UEFA en Nyon acoge este viernes el sorteo de la fase liga de la UEFA Women's Champions League 2026/27. Tras la conclusión de las rondas previas, el Barcelona —vigente campeón tras conquistar su cuarto título continental— y el Real Madrid entran en liza para conocer la hoja de ruta en este torneo de tabla única ampliado a 18 participantes. Cada club disputará seis compromisos (tres en casa y tres a domicilio) midiéndose a dos rivales de cada uno de los tres bombos configurados según el ranking UEFA, con la premisa de no cruzarse con conjuntos de su misma federación nacional. El Barcelona partirá como primer cabeza de serie en el Bombo 1 junto a potencias como el OL Lyonnes, Chelsea, Bayern de Múnich, Arsenal y PSG. Por su parte, el Real Madrid figura en el Bombo 2 al lado de Juventus, Häcken, Roma, Benfica y París FC, evitando a estos clubes pero optando a medirse con gigantes del primer bombo. Paralelamente, también se sorteará la segunda ronda de clasificación de la Copa de Europa, donde la Real Sociedad debutará en la segunda competición continental tras ser eliminada en la previa europea. El sorteo de la fase liga de la UEFA Women's Champions League 2026/27 se celebrará este viernes 4 de septiembre a partir de las 12:00 horas (horario peninsular español) en la sede de la UEFA en Nyon, Suiza. El evento se podrá seguir en directo por televisión e internet en España en abierto mediante la emisión en streaming en UEFA.com y las plataformas oficiales de la UEFA. Sigue al minuto los cruces resultantes del sorteo de la Champions League femenina y toda la actualidad del fútbol europeo en MARCA.com y escucha la retransmisión en directo en Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Marvin Bartley & David Martindale set for reunion as Livingston host Stenhousemuir - watch on BBC Scotland
articles.summary: Stenhousemuir manager Marvin Bartley reveals he has not spoken to Livingston sporting director David Martindale since resigning from the club at the end of last season, with the sides set to meet in Friday's BBC Scotland TV match.
articles.body:
Stenhousemuir manager Marvin Bartley has not spoken to Livingston sporting director David Martindale since resigning from the West Lothian club at the end of last season.

The two sides face each other for the first time in the Scottish Championship on Friday evening in front of the BBC Scotland cameras.

Back in May, Bartley and assistant Neil Hastings said they "had no option but to resign" after being asked to reapply for their positions with Livi.

The former Hibernian, Livingston and Bournemouth midfielder took charge at Almondvale in January, stepping up from a backroom role once Martindale moved into a new position.

"No, I've not seen or spoken to Davie since leaving the football club," said Bartley.

"Obviously, he's got a busy time over the summer in terms of bringing in players. He's busy, I'm busy so I've not spoken to Davie since leaving the football club."

Since his departure, Bartley has been in touch with Livingston chairman Calvin Ford, who sent him a "lovely message" wishing him well after Stenhousemuir edged past Livi on penalties in the League Cup group stage at Ochilview.

And while the nature of his departure stung at the time, the 40-year-old is relishing life with a part-time Stenny side that are still unbeaten after nine matches in all competitions so far this season.

"At the time, I was definitely hurt in the days that followed - but if you're asking me now, my full focus is on Stenhousemuir," says Bartley.

"When the situation happened, I was really, really shocked.

"But the more people I spoke to people about it - and the more people that found out about it who weren't shocked - probably made me realise that I was maybe a little bit naive and green.

"That's probably just me as a person. I take everything at face value.

"Right now, I have got no kind of feeling to it. It's just another chapter in my book and I'm just continuing to try to do the best I possibly can for Stenhousemuir."

Scottish Championship: Livingston v Stenhousemuir

Stenhousemuir have defied expectations with their stellar start to the season. They currently gaze down the table at their Championship rivals after three wins and a draw, the latest a 3-1 victory last weekend over Inverness Caledonian Thistle.

Appointed as Stenny boss when Gary Naysmith - who engineered promotion from League 1 - left to join Ayr United, Bartley has also overseen a successful League Cup group campaign and victory over Premiership side Motherwell, with Hearts up next in next Friday's home quarter-final.

Before that, they face Glenn Whelan's Livingston side, who have won two and lost two of their league matches so far this term.

Fairytales are no stranger to the Championship after the heroics of fellow part-time side Arbroath five years ago. Dick Campbell's Red Lichties pushed Kilmarnock all the way in a dramatic duel for the title.

Do the Warriors dare to dream of battling their way to what would be a mind-boggling double promotion, and top-flight football?

"Every club in the pyramid now dreams of one day being in the top flight," says Bartley.

"There's still so long to go and it's a boring answer for you all, but when I came into the job we spoke about what we hope to achieve and that's not changed.

"We've got that target and it doesn't take a rocket scientist to work out what that target is because everyone had us as favourites to go down in this league and we understand we are only four games into it.

"We can't get carried away with thinking about promotion or play-offs or anything like that because this league is unforgiving.

"We're thinking about achieving our goals and if we do that, that's a minor miracle in itself when you look at the financial constraints we have compared to every other club in this league."

articles.title: Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola started their paths to the top at Antiguoko: 'If I really think about it, it's absolutely crazy'
articles.summary: Born within 15 miles of each other and only seven months apart, the managers of Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool are all products of Antiguoko; Sky Sports visited the tiny Basque club to hear how it all began for Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola
articles.body:
"The centre circle was just over there," says Roberto Montiel, the club's long-serving coach and vice-president, as he takes a seat in what is now a public park. He rubs his thumb and forefinger together as he recalls the texture of the old playing surface.

"The pitch wasn't like the new one up there. It was smaller and made of small stones, like gravel. The balls weren't like the ones now either. When they got wet, they became heavy. You would slip and slide, and if you fell, you'd end up with a terrible scrape."

The games played here by this neighbourhood club's celebrated alumni, two of whom meet as managers when Arsenal face Chelsea on Sky Sports on Sunday, are the stuff of local legend.

"Even then you could see their vision for the game," adds Montiel.

"On this pitch made of gravel, trying to pass those balls when it was raining, with puddles all over the place, with everything getting dirty. Honestly, it was something special to watch. The teams from those '81 and '82 generations were incredible."

Arteta and Iraola played in the latter age group; Alonso the former. "It was like a national team of the best players in the area and it made us an unbeatable team," says Alvaro Parra, a former Antiguoko team-mate and close friend of Arteta's.

"I remember games against Real Sociedad that were so easy. They would come to play us and we would beat them 5-0. Athletic Club would come and we would beat them as well. We won all the leagues. The team became known as the Basque Dream Team."

The club continues to turn out talent. Over at their offices, a mile further into town, near Ondarreta beach, Montiel jokes that they need more wall space to continue displaying signed shirts from a list of top-division graduates that now runs to more than 40 names.

Those of Arteta, Alonso and Iraola hold pride of place.

Their former colleagues are used to their success. But it remains a source of wonder, even to them, that these three Antiguoko players, born within 15 miles of each other, only seven months apart, in Gipuzkoa, the smallest province in Spain, have come this far.

"If I really think about it, it's absolutely crazy that our three friends are managing these Premier League teams," says Parra. "Sometimes I turn on the TV and say, 'Oh, it's Mikel! Oh, it's Xabi! What's happened here?'" adds Mikel Yanguas, another old team-mate.

Arteta: 'He was like a predator on the pitch'

Arteta was the pick of them growing up. "He had something different," says Yanguas, who played as a striker. "He was small but very technical and very clever. He played right behind me and he was always thinking about his next pass. I just needed to run."

Yanguas, who later moved to Barcelona's La Masia academy with Arteta, jokes that his old team-mate made him look better than he was. Parra, a former centre-back, feels similarly. "I just had to pass the ball to Mikel Arteta. Mikel Arteta to Yanguas. Goal."

Montiel is full of stories, many of them set on the old gravel pitch, and many of which highlight Arteta's intelligence, even as a boy. "The one I like to tell, and the one that stays with me most, shows that he was a player who was so alert to everything," he says.

"It was right over there, in midfield. The referee blew for a drop ball, and just as he let it bounce, Arteta flicked it away with the outside of his boot and hit a long pass across the pitch for a team-mate who was on his own to score - and that was against Real Sociedad."

There was an edge to Arteta too - even when playing up a year with Alonso. "He had a real competitive look about him," adds Montiel.

"He was super-attentive to everything you said. He showed an interest in everything. And then, when he went on the pitch, he was a predator. And that was against players a year older. I don't even need to tell you what he was like against players of his own age."

Arteta's competitiveness is one of his defining qualities as a manager. It was evident off the pitch as well as on it growing up.

Montiel remembers Arteta sliding, Jurgen Klinsmann-style, down the hallway of his house in Liverpool after beating him at PlayStation during a visit while he was at Everton.

"Whatever game you played with him, you would always lose," adds Parra. "If you played PlayStation, you would lose. If you played ping pong, you would lose. He was very, very competitive. If you beat him at anything, he would get angry and go home."

Parra chuckles as he utters the last line. He and Arteta were otherwise inseparable, their friendship, and holidays together, continuing even after his career took him abroad.

"After the year he made his debut with Paris Saint-Germain, he called me and said, 'Alvaro, pack your suitcase, we're going to Marbella.'" Parra has no photographs of that trip, lamentably. But he reaches for his phone and flicks through a selection of others.

Parra cherishes the memories. But Arteta, he stresses, was also organised and disciplined, in all aspects of his life, including his studies. "His parents instilled that in him."

Those qualities helped when he made the move to Barcelona aged only 15. Yanguas, although similarly talented according to those who first spotted him playing on La Concha beach with Arteta, never settled and returned home the following year.

"Mikel had a better capacity to adapt," he says. "He was quickly speaking to the other people at La Masia. I think he demonstrated that in other countries too, in France, in Scotland, in England. He always had the ability to adapt to any environment."

Iraola: 'A great team-mate and quiet leader'

Back in Berio, we have moved up the slope from the site of Antiguoko's old pitch to their new one, where an U16s team are being put through their paces under the midday sun.

"This is a very good group," says Montiel, before gesturing towards a slight figure in central midfield who stands out for his technical quality. "He had an offer from Real Sociedad but preferred to stay with us," he adds, with more than a hint of pride.

Real Sociedad and Athletic are signing Antiguoko players at ever-younger ages, Montiel says. But for some, the education on offer at Antiguoko is reason to stay. The coach overseeing this session, Iñigo Iraola, cousin of Andoni, is certainly from good footballing stock.

Like the older Iraola, who returned to Antiguoko as a coach while studying for his badges following his playing career, Iñigo came through the club's youth ranks as a player.

"The first game I ever watched was here in Berio, when Andoni came back with Athletic Club as an U18," he says. "From then on I always saw him as a role model and an example to follow."

He remembers Andoni taking him to buy his first pair of football boots. "They were Adidas boots," he says, smiling. "I went to buy them with him on my birthday here in San Sebastian. He was already playing for Athletic, so it was special for me to go with him."

Iraola is remembered differently to Arteta as a boy at Antiguoko.

"Mikel was captain of the team, he took responsibility," says Parra. "Andoni was more introverted, but at the same time he had incredible ability, and even if he was quieter, he was always a fun and polite guy, a great team-mate, and popular in the group."

"He was one of my favourites," adds Montiel. "Playing out wide, he didn't get as many touches as those in the centre, but every time he got to the byline, he would beat two or three players, make a pass and we'd score. He could work wonders with the ball."

He had the same competitive streak as Arteta. And although he was more reserved, as Parra explains, he had his moments.

"In our team, he played as a right winger and had a really important role," says Parra. "But when he went to Athletic, their manager Ernesto Valverde moved him to full-back.

"At first, he didn't like it at all. He even got angry, asking, 'Why are you putting me in defence?' But Valverde knew he was going to be an incredible full-back because he had the quality and the ability to take on players and get all the way up the pitch."

Iraola's leadership abilities emerged later, first as captain of Athletic, where he ended up making 510 appearances, then as a manager.

"One thing I really admire about Andoni is the kind of leader he is," says his cousin. "He isn't going to raise his voice above everyone else. He's a quieter, understated kind of leader who has more of an impact through the example he sets his players every day."

Ignacio Azpilicueta likes to joke that he had the best view in football.

As the central defender who occupied the space directly behind Alonso at Antiguoko, he enjoyed a front-row seat as his teenaged team-mate began to find his passing range.

"He played as the midfield pivot right in front of me, so I had the privilege of seeing Xabi's best passes from my position, right at the point when he developed the physical power and ball-striking ability that he went on to show for so many years."

Alonso had always been a good player. "He won the ball back a lot, played with two feet, and all of his passes were good," says Montiel. Azpilicueta recalls friends commenting on Alonso's ability during intra-school tournaments on La Concha beach.

He would come alive on the pitch. "He was really passionate," says Yanguas. "He really lived the game." But starting out at Antiguoko, few felt stardom beckoned for him.

"I remember our first sessions together and I would say I don't remember feeling that he was going to become the football star he is today," says Azpilicueta, who is no relation to the former Chelsea defender of the same name but had a good career of his own.

"He had a good touch, but physically he wasn't by any means the biggest or the strongest or the quickest. It took him a while to grow."

His trajectory, both physically and in terms of his career, changed in his U17 year. "I would say that was the moment when he really took off," says Azpilicueta. "He'd always had that intelligence, but now it was accompanied by that physical development."

"At that age, you could see he was going to be a first division player," says Parra. "Maybe not that he was going to win the Champions League, but you could see was going to be a top-level player."

According to Azpilicueta, he also benefitted from the qualities of humility and intelligence evident in Arteta and Iraola.

"I would say he was a very normal kid, like the rest of us. He didn't stand out in any particular way. He had a sense of humour. He was a good friend to his friends. But above all, he was very intelligent. He always made good decisions, on and off the pitch.

"I would say that has been a big part of his success."

So how does this little club do it? Arteta, Alonso and Iraola are of course their best-known graduates but more recent ones include Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi, their second World Cup winner after Alonso, and Rayo Vallecano boss Iñigo Perez.

Some point to the club's scouting in the area - "Oscar Landa, our sporting director, has a 95 per cent success rate," says Montiel - others to the atmosphere created by the longevity and commitment of their staff. But it usually comes back to the same thing.

"We've never changed the DNA of Antiguoko," says Montiel. "Competitive instinct, intensity and sporting discipline are non-negotiable." It is surely no coincidence that his old mentee Arteta uses that same term in reference to his managerial philosophy.

"We try to instil the values of sacrifice, discipline, hard work, teamwork and competitiveness," adds Iñigo Iraola. "I think it also reflects what the Basque player is: dedicated and committed to working hard every day. I think that's what makes us special."

Arteta, Alonso and Iraola personify those traits, as much managers as they did as players.

"The results should be seen in sporting terms, but also in human terms," says the club's general director Gorka Azpeita. "Beyond the footballing talent they have, it's important to highlight what they're like as people. They should be seen for the values they have, the people they are, and how it's enabled them to get where they are."

The only remaining question, then, is who they will be rooting for when Arteta and Alonso go head to head some 600 miles away in north London on Sunday. "That's like choosing between Mum and Dad," says Azpeita, laughing. "A draw would be perfect."

articles.title: "Este es el Mourinho que necesitaba el Real Madrid"
articles.standfirst: Amalio Moratalla analiza en La Tribu el sorprendente cambio del técnico portugués en su segunda etapa en el banquillo blanco
articles.summary: Amalio Moratalla analiza en La Tribu el sorprendente cambio del técnico portugués en su segunda etapa en el banquillo blanco
articles.body: Amalio Moratalla, Pedro Riesco, Ricardo Reyes, Ferran Martínez y Pablo Pinto han sido los tertulianos de este viernes en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la nueva versión de Mourinho y la previa de una nueva jornada de Liga. José Mourinho está mostrando una versión diferente en su regreso al Real Madrid. Más tranquilo, positivo y alejado, al menos por el momento, del perfil más combativo que marcó buena parte de su primera etapa en el Santiago Bernabéu. Un cambio que fue objeto de debate en La Tribu. Pedro Riesco reconoció su sorpresa por lo visto hasta ahora. "Me está sorprendiendo Mourinho. Está pasando una luna de miel en el Real Madrid. Es un Mourinho sorprendentemente positivo, muy pausado. Para el Real Madrid es bueno tener a una persona que dé equilibrio", explicó. Eso sí, Riesco espera comprobar cómo reacciona el portugués cuando aparezcan los primeros problemas: "En algún momento saldrá ese Mourinho. Veremos cuando no vengan bien dadas. En luna de miel, top". Ricardo Reyes también destacó las diferencias respecto al entrenador que se conocía hasta ahora: "No sé si la vida le ha cambiado, si es diferente. De momento, este Mourinho es muy distinto al que conocíamos". Además, valoró su actuación en uno de los asuntos que ha rodeado al equipo: "En el tema Asencio, hizo lo que tenía que hacer". Amalio Moratalla fue especialmente contundente a la hora de valorar el cambio del portugués. "En la otra etapa no dio tregua. Sabe que en este momento no funciona la guerrilla. Tiene suficiente autoridad en el vestuario sabiendo que está puesto por el presidente", señaló. Para Moratalla, Mourinho ha entendido cuál es el camino que debe seguir con esta plantilla: "Cree que a este grupo le tiene que hacer rendir por la vía de sumar una familia que compita. Estoy encantado con este Mourinho. Este es el Mourinho que necesitaba el Madrid". Ferran Martínez también incidió en esa transformación: "Mucho más pausado. En su primera etapa se le fichó como un anti-Guardiola. Esta vez ha venido no para cargarse a nadie, ni acabar con ningún proyecto. Le veo más maduro". El periodista incluso apuntó a que esta nueva oportunidad puede haber cambiado la manera en la que Mourinho afronta su regreso al club blanco: "No sé si esta oportunidad ha sido un regalo inesperado para él. Conoce la casa, el presidente y se lo toma de otra manera, con más filosofía. Está de vuelta. Lo veo disfrutón y más abuelo que padre". Pablo Pinto, por su parte, recordó que este perfil tampoco es completamente desconocido en la trayectoria del portugués. "Mourinho también es este. Este Mourinho gracioso, irónico y con sorna se ha visto en otros momentos de su carrera". Una versión de Mourinho que, de momento, convence en La Tribu. El gran interrogante, como apuntó Pedro Riesco, llegará cuando termine la "luna de miel" y al Real Madrid no le vengan tan bien dadas.

articles.title: Jude Bellingham: England midfielder looks ready to show full potential at Real Madrid
articles.summary: Jude Bellingham looks fit and ready to build on his World Cup form as he aims to rediscover his best at Real Madrid under Jose Mourinho.
articles.body:
Jude Bellingham has started the new season looking like a player with something to prove.

The 23-year-old's two goals and three assists have helped Real Madrid to an impressive start under new boss Jose Mourinho, with three wins from as many games.

Bellingham's performances, and the freedom he has been given in his new role, has attracted a lot of attention.

By playing higher up the pitch, he looks more free, more influential and closer to the role in which he first made such an impact at the Bernabeu in his debut 2023-24 season, where he scored 23 goals as his side won La Liga and the Champions League.

Bellingham's last two campaigns were less consistent, with his displays and attacking influence affected not only by a deeper role, but by recurring injuries. He had a long-standing shoulder problem that required surgery in 2025 and a hamstring issue that kept him out for 10 matches in 2026.

Now, however, he appears to be at peak fitness, ready to build on his impressive World Cup form for England and showcase the full extent of his talent.

Since returning this summer to take charge of the club for a second spell, Mourinho has made an important adjustment in reducing the defensive workload that previously meant Bellingham had to cover huge areas of the pitch.

"We've organised the team differently," he said after Real Madrid's 4-0 La Liga win over Malaga.

"Bellingham sometimes defended like a second left-back last season. I told him I do not want to see that anymore. I made a deal with him."

The Portuguese manager has used Bellingham primarily as a number 10 in a 4-2-3-1 system, operating behind French striker Kylian Mbappe and with the freedom to move across the attacking line.

That gives the England midfielder a clearer role. Rather than constantly moving between midfield, defence and attack, he can spend more time in the areas where he is most dangerous.

"For me, this is his position, with his connection with the forwards, he can score goals," added Mourinho.

"He has to play close to the goal. Playing at number six or number eight, we're losing his closeness to the goal. I like this Jude."

It has meant Bellingham can receive the ball between the lines, carry it forward, combine with the forwards and make late runs into the penalty area.

Just as importantly, he is being given greater freedom to decide when to move.

Bellingham has explained the difference himself in an interview with Real Madrid TV.

"I feel more free to decide when to drop back, when to stay up or when to get into the box," he said. "I think this is the best position for me."

Mourinho still expects him to press and recover possession, but the difference is where that work begins.

Instead of dropping deep towards his own penalty area, Bellingham can now use his energy to press opponents higher up the pitch.

When Madrid win the ball, he is already closer to the forwards. That allows him to connect midfield with attack and provide another player who can combine with Mbappe and Vinicius Jr.

It also explains why Mourinho has been keen to stress Madrid's attacking players must work together rather than operate as individuals.

"The team dynamic is about 11, not 2+9," he said.

The midfielder also described working with Mourinho as a "dream", having previously only met the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham manager once before his appointment.

There is clearly an early understanding and respect between the two.

Mourinho has repeatedly spoken about Bellingham's importance to his plans, describing him as a "unique and super important player" with qualities that include physical, mental and tactical.

He also suggested Bellingham should be one of the players in the running for the Ballon d'Or.

"He is a unique kind of player and extremely important for the team," said Mourinho.

"His mental strength, tactical ability, the way he recovers the ball, the way he pressures, the way he plays up front, I am very happy."

'I'm having a lot of fun, really enjoying my football'

For Mourinho, that versatility is part of what makes Bellingham so valuable. He can press, recover possession, score, contribute in the air and drive the team forward.

The Real boss has also pointed to Thomas Tuchel's use of Bellingham at the World Cup as an example of how to get the best out of him.

Bellingham was one of England's standout players, finishing with seven goals and an assist in his eight appearances, and his attacking qualities were allowed to flourish.

That experience also appears to have given the player a confidence boost, particularly as he rejoined Madrid later than most of his team-mates and had less time to prepare for the new campaign.

Although Real's three league wins - scoring 10 goals and conceding two - are only a small sample, and the demands will increase as the season progresses amid Champions League football, the early signs are very positive.

For Bellingham, whose huge strength has always been his ability to affect almost every part of a game, Mourinho's system has given him more control over where that influence is used.

After a difficult couple of seasons following the high standards he set in his first year, the England midfielder is enjoying his football again.

"I'm having a lot of fun, I'm really enjoying my football, and that's why I'm performing well," he told club media.

If he continues in this vein with Mourinho's continued support, it could turn out to be his best season yet.

articles.title: How Motherwell's blueprint is defying second-season syndrome
articles.summary: New faces, same identity. Motherwell's approach has fans dreaming of a campaign that surpasses the highs of 2025-26.
articles.body:
Motherwell secure a place in Europe and serve up the best football their fanbase has ever experienced - but at what cost?

They lose their transformational manager after just a year in charge and have the spine ripped out of their team.

So then arrives an unknown face in the dugout, 35-year-old Alfred Johansson, and 11 new players.

Supporters of provincial sides have long been conditioned into fearing second-season syndrome after enjoying a year of fun but Motherwell continue to defy traditional Scottish football thinking.

Now supporters of the fan-owned Fir Park club are dreaming of a campaign that surpasses the highs of 2025-26.

Motherwell demolish 10-man Dundee Utd to extend unbeaten start

Who has your Premiership club brought in & let go this summer?

It is difficult to comprehend how one man can influence one club over such a short period of time, but the impact of Jens Berthel Askou , now head coach of Toulouse in Ligue 1, has gone beyond Lanarkshire.

In relation to what can be achieved in Scotland on a modest budget, Dundee United boss Jim Goodwin said the Dane's work in the Scottish Premiership has given "guys like myself a bit of a wake-up call".

Goodwin's 10-man side were pulled apart by Johansson's iteration of Motherwell on Wednesday, extending their unbeaten league start after four games, but a noticeable shift in United's style has clearly been inspired by Askou.

There has been no style shift at Fir Park, though. No matter the coach, no matter the players, the club now have an identity that has been responsible for a huge spike in attendances, as well as the on-field results.

Speaking at an event for the Well Society, Motherwell's 4,000-strong fan-ownership group, vice-captain Stephen O'Donnell detailed how the club's continuity has benefited the squad.

"If the new manager was a 'heid it and kick it' manager, we'd all be in a right pickle," the defender said. "I definitely wouldn't be playing centre-back anymore."

Out of Askou's first-choice XI last term, only four have started a Premiership game this season, whether that is through players departing or injuries.

Goalkeeper Calum Ward and centre-back pairing Stephen Welsh and Paul McGinn were fundamental to the club setting a new clean-sheet milestone and achieving the second-best defensive record in their top-flight history.

Ward left for Queens Park Rangers, McGinn is recovering from long-term injury, and Welsh is now at Championship leaders Swansea with Elijah Just, who became Motherwell's top transfer sale in July, just a year after Udinese's Lennon Miller had set the previous record.

Elliot Watt, arguably the Premiership's standout midfielder last term, also exited for Samsunspor in Turkey, while Callum Slattery left for Sheffield Wednesday after his contract expired.

Scottish Premiership: Rangers v Motherwell

Listen to live match commentary on BBC Sounds, watch highlights on BBC iPlayer and follow text updates on the BBC Sport website and app

Motherwell are providing a blueprint for other Scottish sides following an unprecedented period of transfer income totalling more than £10m across the past year.

That seems to have opened the door for the club to shop in a better market this summer but there is also now enough evidence for players joining to know the future rewards that can come with impressing at Fir Park.

Midfielder Joe Hodge, regarded as the Watt replacement, was playing in Portugal's top flight last term and centre-back Martin Moormann was playing in the Austrian Bundesliga, while reported six-figure signing Jardell Kanga will hope to fill the void left by World Cup breakout star Just .

Even the appointment of Johansson was eye-catching given his previous, and only, job in management was a two-and-a-half-year spell at 26-time Norwegian title winners Rosenborg.

And the early indicators are hugely encouraging. The Swede is showing signs he can take last season's fringe players to a new level while finally unlocking the potential of Rangers academy graduate Alex Lowry, who will return to Ibrox on Saturday.

Motherwell will need to deal with the fact they have not won major silverware since 1991 for at least another eight months after a rotated side suffered a shock League Cup defeat at second-tier Stenhousemuir.

A manic 3-3 draw against St Mirren, during which Johansson's men conceded three times in the space of 10 minutes, came following a hectic and ultimately unsuccessful Conference League qualification attempt that still provided memorable moments against HB Torshavn, HJK Helsinki and Freiburg.

With eight points from four league fixtures, their tally for this season is already double what it was last term at this stage.

It took until late September for Motherwell to get their first Premiership win under Askou last year while they worked through teething issues.

Those 12 months under the Dane meant Johansson took over a squad already ingrained in playing in the way he sees the game but what has he actually changed?

To the eye, not a lot. The former Copenhagen youth coach said he only wanted to tweak the cogs in a well-oiled machine when he was appointed.

Motherwell are more or less still playing with a fluid 4-4-2 formation in and out of possession, with rotations remaining an integral part of their approach.

One difference fans were quick to notice, though, was Johansson's team playing with more width and more intensity on the ball, with crosses from wide areas becoming more frequent as marauding left-back Emmanuel Longelo's influence grows after an excellent debut season in Scotland.

The sample size under the young Swedish manager is still small in comparison to Askou's, but average possession is almost identical, just below the 60% mark.

At this early stage, the data says Johansson's side are scoring, shooting and passing more, but Askou's freakish defensive numbers will take some beating.

Next up for the thriving Lanarkshire club is a short hop to Ibrox on Saturday (15:00 BST), where they have won in three of their past four visits.

That a once-dreaded trip is now relished says it all about the mood around Motherwell.
