articles.title: La Asamblea del Barça será el 19 de septiembre: presentará un récord histórico de ingresos de mil millones
articles.standfirst: Los socios deberán decidir si aprueban la ampliación del crédito para el Espai Barça
articles.summary: Los socios deberán decidir si aprueban la ampliación del crédito para el Espai Barça
articles.body: La Junta Directiva del Barcelona publica este viernes el orden de día de la Asamblea General Ordinaria de socios que celebrará, según acordó ayer, el sábado 19 de septiembre. En la cita, que será telemática, los compromisarios culés deberán aprobar, entre otras medidas, la ampliación del crédito para la conclusión del Espai Barça y el Spotify Camp Nou. Laporta presentará, además, unos beneficios de la 25-26 memorables. El encuentro virtual servirá para que la Junta de Laporta dé a conocer unos números de récord: el club azulgrana presentará las cuentas anuales de la temporada 2025/26, que tienen unos resultados ordinarios positivos por tercera temporada consecutiva y en la que se lograron 1.000 millones de euros de ingresos por primera vez en la historia de la entidad culé. Este extraordinario importe se debe, especialmente, a la explotación de las instalaciones del Spotify Camp Nou, a las que regresó en noviembre del año pasado. "Esta cifra se debe, esencialmente, a la mejora de los ingresos derivados de la explotación del Estadio, pese al hecho de haber jugado algunos partidos durante el primer semestre tanto en el Estadi Johan Cruyff como en el Estadi Olímpic, y algunos partidos en el Spotify Camp Nou con un aforo de 42.000 espectadores. La cifra de ingresos es especialmente relevante porque, pese a estas circunstancias, se ha alcanzado prácticamente el presupuesto previsto para el ejercicio, que contemplaba comenzar la temporada en el Estadio y con un aforo superior a los 60.000 espectadores desde el inicio. Este hecho reafirma el gran potencial futuro del Spotify Camp Nou una vez funcione a pleno rendimiento", explica el Barcelona en un comunicado. "Otros factores que también han contribuido a este récord de ingresos han sido el aumento continuado de los ingresos de patrocinadores y el récord de facturación por la venta de merchandising del Club a través de la filial BLM", añade el texto. Así mismo, los dirigentes oficializarán ante sus socios el presupuesto del ejercicio 2026-27, que superará 1.100. Pero, además, los compromisarios deberán votar para la aprobación o no de la ampliación del crédito para la conclusión del Espai Barça que rondará los 500 millones de euros y también deberán pronunciarse sobre la emisión de bonos garantizados con derechos audiovisuales adicionales del Barcelona. En la Asamblea del día 19, la Mesa quedará constituida en el Auditori 1899 del Spotify Camp Nou, se ratificará también, como recogen los puntos del orden del día, como directivos a Rafa Yuste, Josep Cubells, Alfons Castro, Josep Ignasi Macià, Àngel Riudalbas, Joan Solé y Sisco Pujol, que gestionaron y lideraron al Barcelona desde el 9 de febrero cuando Joan Laporta dimitió con nueve directivos más para presentarse a la reelección a la presidencia.

articles.title: Keith Andrews exclusive: Brentford head coach on the improvements he hopes can help the Bees 'break the ceiling' and reach Europe
articles.summary: Sky Sports exclusive: After Brentford missed out on a place in Europe in the final seconds of the 2025/26 Premier League season, head coach Keith Andrews discusses planning how the Bees can take the next step this season
articles.body:
They were drawing 1-1 with Liverpool at Anfield and knew that one goal would be enough to finish seventh and secure Europa League football.

In the 10th minute of added time, Mikkel Damsgaard dropped the ball off to Vitaly Janelt on the left-hand side of the penalty area. The midfielder hit a cross first time that curled in the most inviting way to the centre of the box.

Kevin Schade was waiting for it, but Dango Ouattara got there first - and steered it off target.

Keith Andrews put his head in his hands and sank to his knees. His first season as a head coach had nearly ended in the most perfect way.

"I felt that epitomised the journey we'd been on last season, with how we started the season, how we grew into the season," he says, reflecting on that moment just over three months on.

"Everybody was so engrossed in our journey and gave absolutely everything. There was no shame at all from not getting into Europe, but it whetted the appetite pretty nicely for how we would do things going into pre-season.

"I sat on holiday and had a chance to think about things with immense pride at what we'd achieved. The next thought, very quickly, was how and where we go again."

Speaking to Sky Sports that day, he promised improvement in 2026/27. "This is a baseline," he said. "We'll continue to push hard."

Around a fortnight after that Sunday at Anfield, Andrews was back at base.

"There's amazing thinking time you don't normally get on a weekly basis to plan and look at things in a more forensic way," he says.

"You look to improve how we train, how we prepare, what the squad feels like, what the dynamic feels like. Everything where you feel we can get a little bit better.

"I felt like we didn't need huge meetings about what this season will be, I just felt it was there day-to-day. You could smell it, you could feel it."

The first major change came on June 12 with the appointment of his former Republic of Ireland team-mate Damien Duff as his assistant.

"He's an unbelievable support for me on a daily basis. You've got to be very impactful in your role and whatever responsibilities you have and Damien is certainly that."

The squad planning stage came next and, after an intense summer in 2025, this one was a lot less so.

Star players Bryan Mbeumo and Christian Norgaard were sold to Manchester United and Arsenal respectively, while Yoane Wissa's eventual departure to Newcastle was protracted and disruptive.

There were no headline sales this year. In fact, the only first-team exits were those of Ethan Pinnock - who only played four times in the Premier League last season - and Frank Onyeka - who had spent the best part of two seasons away from west London - to Coventry for less than £12m.

"At certain stages last season, we just lacked that little bit at senior experience in the squad, different options within games to change it," Andrews says.

"We always try to find a way of competing and our players gave absolutely everything last season, but at times they probably needed a little bit more help.

"The way we've gone about our transfers this summer has been very precise. Jannik [Schuster] is a centre-back with a younger age profile and has slotted into the club really well, Callum Wilson and Jaidon Anthony have proven Premier League quality with experience, so it's not just on the pitch, it's off it in terms of what they bring.

"Mamadou Sangare was an eye-catching signing and he's started really well in our shirt. And the latest one is Malick [Diouf] from West Ham, who we were delighted to be able to get into the building.

"We've added to an already really good squad, we've added very well and we've kept hold of exactly who we wanted to keep hold of. I'm really, really happy with the deals we've got done."

Andrews often speaks about getting better - and is open about the fact that getting better than last season means reaching Europe: "Naturally, the next step for us is to try and break that ceiling."

He will, no doubt, field questions on that topic in press conferences for many months to come.

"The next level of development of individuals," he says.

"Pick a player… Michael Kayode. He had an amazing season, let's get him better. You make all your players better, you feed them that confidence, you create that environment, which we do create. It's inevitable if someone is as humble and hungry as Michael, they will get better.

"Players getting better naturally improves the team. Then you look at each phase of the game.

"At set-pieces we look a real threat, we look really dominant at the moment and we want to continue that.

"How do we create chances? The game is about scoring at one end and keeping goals out at the other, so how do you create opportunities? We want to create opportunities in different ways and not just be a predictable team that can only do it one way.

"And how do we become better without the ball? Are we pressing aggressively high? Can we sit in deep and absorb pressure and be a transition threat, but defend our box with aggression and collective spirit?

"They are just some examples about how we want to take the next step."

So far, that next step is beginning to take shape.

On the opening weekend, they welcomed Tottenham to the Gtech Community Stadium - and blew Roberto De Zerbi's side away.

They won 3-0, but it would have been four had Igor Thiago not rolled his penalty onto the base of the left-hand post.

Analysing the game afterwards, Sky Sports ' Jamie Redknapp was impressed by what he saw.

"When somebody was out of position, they just found a way to fill the right areas. They are incredibly brave at the back, the two centre-backs play so high and press you, stop you getting out," he said.

"What Roberto De Zerbi said beforehand was that they were going to deal with a lot of long balls today, but what they actually dealt with was total football.

"It can mean different things when I hear that said," Andrews responds.

"When I think about that in terms of how we play the game, we can play in different ways. We can control games now with the ability we have as a team, the quality we have technically as a team.

"The individuals are flourishing within the squad and how we're playing, then if teams want to have a fight, we'll have a fight.

"We've got so many different attributes within the squad where we can cause the opposition problems in an unpredictable way, but we always respect every phase of the game and try and respect the opposition where we try to nullify their strengths and see if we can outdo them."

It was an evening to remember for Andrews.

"Firstly, we need to start with the fans. I thought the flags [organised by fan group TW8 Casuals] and the energy as the players came in from their warm-up and pre-game was pretty special.

"It felt energetic, it felt edgy. I loved the intentions of our fans straightaway in that game. I felt they could sense us producing a performance.

"I was confident the players would. You never truly know. I thought the connection between the players and the fans was really special and we maintained it throughout."

A 6-1 thumping of Birmingham in the Carabao Cup followed, before a 1-1 draw against Leeds at Elland Road last weekend, during which he felt Schade should have been awarded a penalty after a trip by Jayden Bogle in the box.

Sunderland's visit to the capital is up next on Saturday afternoon.

"We're in a good place, there's no denying that. The players are playing freely, with a lot of verve and personality, which I really like.

"The only way you keep that going is keeping striving, keeping pushing each other, being very demanding of each other. It's a good place to be demanding of each other when you play so well and with such an edge.

"Nothing is given in this league, but we can push the group more, they can push each other to see how far we can go."

They came within one goal of Europe at Anfield. Andrews wants to make sure Brentford get even closer this time.

articles.title: Andy McCann interview: The assistant headteacher from Liverpool about to become England manager for a week
articles.summary: Cheshire League manager - and assistant headteacher - Andy McCann discusses preparing to become England manager for a week and leading his side into the UEFA Regions Cup intermediate round, where they will face Finland, Portugal and Sweden for a place at next summer's finals...
articles.body:
By day, he works as an assistant headteacher at Great Sankey High School in Warrington. The summer holidays have come to a conclusion and the school year is back in full swing.

But he is about to take eight days off in order to become England manager... sort of.

That's because McCann is also the manager of the Cheshire League, a representative team made up of the best players from the Cheshire League Premier Division.

His side won the FA Inter-League Cup by beating the Herts Senior County League at Leicester's King Power Stadium on May 9 - and, in doing so, earned the chance to represent England in the UEFA Regions Cup.

So, first things first, what is the Regions Cup?

It is an amateur tournament founded in 1996 and held every two years since 1999 - barring 2021 due to Covid.

Teams from the nations taking part either qualify or are nominated, before entering the intermediate round, where they are split into eight groups. The winners of those groups then progress to the finals.

Spain have won it four times, Italy three, Poland two, and the Republic of Ireland, Portugal, Croatia and the Czech Republic once each.

On Sunday September 6, McCann and Co fly out to Sweden for three games and the chance to become the first England team ever to progress to the finals.

"During the Inter-League Cup, the chairman Rob Goodwin-Davey - who is Mr Cheshire League - kept saying to me there was a chance we could go and represent England, but I wasn't really thinking about that. I was purely focused on trying to win the cup," he tells Sky Sports.

"As a management team, we met up a few times to go through final details, tactics, set-pieces and it was then we started to realise it was quite big.

"But once we won it, people in the pub were saying to me: 'Once the World Cup's out the way, you're England manager!'

"Without wanting to compare it too much to 'real life', this job is a bit like being an international manager, albeit a much lower level.

"I'm sure it will dawn on me when we board the flight, but it's a real privilege and an honour to be England manager for a week, at whatever level. We've worked out we're the England D team, so we'll take that!"

They are not just England by name, though.

"When we get to the airport, we get the full England kit. So whatever you've seen England wearing at the World Cup, it's exactly the same. The boys get a full tracksuit, three t-shirts, three training shirts, three pairs of shorts, three pairs of socks - and we will play in the full England kit.

"A lot of the lads are buzzing for that alone. You have your captains and drivers who are keeping everyone focused on winning the competition, but for some of the lads, just being able to pull the shirt on in a competitive game is massive."

What differentiates the Cheshire League from their professional counterparts, however, is that they are all amateur players with day jobs.

Among them are captain Tim Kinsella, who is an electrician, and vice-captain Liam McDowell, who is a quantity surveyor. Two members of the squad are qualified PE teachers, others are studying PGCEs to become teachers.

"Some lads are having to take unpaid leave, but the majority are taking it as normal leave and just treating it as an opportunity to have eight days off and enjoy it," McCann adds.

"We haven't had any issues with anyone not able to travel, but it was a concern.

"In the preparation for the final, as a bit of a motivator, I guaranteed the final squad that if we won, they would be the squad I'd take to Sweden. I felt it was right and I've stuck to that.

"The only one missing is Juliano Rosa Silva, who played every minute of the cup, but is injured. He is heartbroken he can't play."

The reality of football at this level is that scouting the opposition is tricky at best.

"For the first game, we've got an FA-registered coach who will be helping out, but his main priority is watching the other teams, so when we play on Monday, he's going to go and watch the other two.

"For the second and third games, we'll know a lot more, as I'm sure they will too, and we'll be a lot more prepared. For the first game, we'll be focused on what got us to the King Power and what helped us win it.

"We've built a team that we feel is quite unique in the way we approached it. Without giving too much away, there are probably more technical players in the Cheshire League than what we've picked, but we've picked a team that is to our strengths and we've got a lot of power and pace in the team."

Laying in wait for McCann's side are representative teams from Finland (Jarvenpaa United), Portugal (Algarve) and Sweden (Gothenburg). Of the 34 teams taking part, they are ranked 11th, 7th and 30th respectively; Cheshire League are ranked 17th.

This may be an amateur team, but the preparation for this adventure has been as professional as possible.

"We're just very focused. For now, that's the next step," adds McCann.

"We've done everything we can. We've got the full eight days planned down to the hour. Rest, recovery, recuperation, we've got down the times we're eating, we've mirrored training with game times. If you're going to do it, you do it to the best of your ability.

"In the build-up to the final, Rob got three of the Mid-Cheshire team that won the Inter-League Cup in 2004 to do a speech after the last training session, which was really nice. I met two of them over the summer holidays and asked them about what they felt was good about the trip and I've listened to them and put some things into place.

"We're not going just to enjoy it and be England for seven days, but get beaten. The focus is winning all three games and getting to the finals, but I also see this as a chance to raise the profile for the next generation. It's massive."

Once the trip to Sweden is over, McCann will be back up at the crack of dawn, teaching the next generation - and, all being well, it will be as an England hero… sort of.​​​

articles.title: Louisiana Judge Rules Against NCAA, Clearing Path for Former NFL Players to Join LSU Roster
articles.summary: BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — LSU coach Lane Kiffin's chances of fielding former NFL players improved Thursday night when a Louisiana judge issued a preliminary injunction against the NCAA in a high-profile eligibility case.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — LSU coach Lane Kiffin's chances of fielding former NFL players improved Thursday night when a Louisiana judge issued a preliminary injunction against the NCAA in a high-profile eligibility case.

East Baton Rouge Parish Judge William Jorden issued his ruling the night before LSU was due to submit its 105-man roster to the Southeastern Conference, which last week announced heavy potential punishment for football and basketball teams that bring in ex-pros.

The ruling clears the way for LSU to list some former NFL players on its roster. How many games they might be eligible to play remains to be seen as the matter continues working its way through the courts.

"It's not about coach Kiffin. It's not about LSU. It's about treating these kids fairly," said Tony Clayton, an attorney for the athletes. "Today, justice was served. And justice was serve to the SEC. It was served like a cold cup of gumbo. And that judge forced them to eat it."

The ruling followed a nearly nine-hour hearing in a courtroom less than three miles from the LSU campus. Several athletes took the stand to explain why they should be allowed to return to play college sports for a fifth season — some of them after turning pro.

The commissioner of the powerful SEC argued against them, and the league doubled down by filing a lawsuit against the school in a federal court in Alabama. That lawsuit could become the SEC's best chance at preventing former pros from playing this season.

Thursday's hearing was attended by Louisiana attorney general Liz Murrill, who filed an athlete-friendly brief in the case. While she did not make any arguments in court, she spoke after the hearing and referred to the SEC's federal lawsuit against LSU as "legal garbage," and "frivolous."

"We're going to continue to do everything we can to protect the school from those threats," she said.

The courtroom confrontation came just two days before 11th-ranked LSU opens the season at home against Clemson. Jorden scheduled the hearing over his temporary injunction preventing the NCAA from barring former pros or fifth-year college athletes, a stance reiterated by the SEC and other Power Four conferences in potential punishments adopted last week.

"Lane Kiffin is cold as ice. He's wonderful to watch. He pushes every limit to try to win," said New Orleans attorney Jason Williams, representing the SEC. "The SEC exists in part to prevent individual competitive incentives from destroying the common conditions that make college football great."

Former NFL players testify about modest pay in pros

Former New Orleans Saints defensive lineman Zxavian Harris and former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright, two players who now expect to suit up for LSU within weeks, sat next to each other in the gallery as the hearing began. Both took the stand to say they would not have signed with NFL teams this year had they known they might get another year in college.

Each said they each earned about $1 million in college. Harris said he was paid just $190 in travel expenses by the Saints and spent all of his time with the club rehabbing a foot injury. Wright said he was paid a $25,000 signing bonus by Philadelphia before his brief time with the Browns and would gladly pay that back for the chance to play for LSU.

While both former Mississippi players were unsure how soon they might make their LSU debut, they said after the hearing that they expect to play when the Tigers visit Ole Miss on Sept. 19.

Two LSU soccer players, Jazmin Ferguson and Jocelyn Ollivierre, won earlier court orders and have already played this season. Ferguson testified that she was paid $4,500 by a USL team, but ended her contract and paid the money back in hopes of clearing the way to play for the Tigers again. Two LSU softball players also testified.

The athletes were questioned after SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey was on the stand for more than two hours, defending the league's authority to enforce its longstanding rules barring former pros from returning to play at its 16 member schools — and enforce newly outlined fines and suspensions against programs and coaches. He said school presidents and chancellors felt that they needed to establish ways to hold schools accountable for recruiting professionals back to college.

"The line between professional sports and college sports needs to be maintained," Sankey testified, adding that the league was concerned about incoming athletes being displaced from limited roster spots.

As he spoke, the SEC filed the federal lawsuit in Alabama against LSU and its leadership, alleging the school had "waged a deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes" in defiance of league rules. The court filing against one of the league's founding members in 1933 seeks an injunction barring LSU from violating the SEC's First Amendment rights by forcing it to "associate with conduct that is contrary to the conference's purpose and mission."

While questioning Sankey, attorneys for the athletes cited numerous examples of when SEC eligibility rules align with NCAA rules, suggesting the potential for collusion. They questioned why league members met last week to adopt stiff penalties for the very actions addressed in the Louisiana state court's temporary injunction against the NCAA.

The attorneys also asked why the SEC singled out players who signed contracts with specific U.S.-based leagues — the NFL, NBA and WNBA — but not overseas pro leagues or women's pro soccer leagues. When Sankey tried to qualify an answer about whether the SEC had previously punished a school for adding a player with previous pro experience, Clayton said, "I didn't ask how to build a clock. I'm just asking what time it is."

Sankey acknowledged that there had previously been no such punishment, but that it had been considered against Alabama last basketball season when the Crimson Tide briefly added a former G League player.

Players going to court has become common

The players in question also include former Denver Broncos defensive back Blake Cotton, who like Harris and Wright is hoping to join LSU and Kiffin.

Wright started practicing at LSU this week, too late to be eligible for Saturday's home opener against Clemson under the NCAA's required seven days of practice. Harris has committed to LSU, while Cotton, who played at Utah last fall, has been recruited by Kiffin.

All three are among a host of athletes who've argued in lawsuits around the country that they are unfairly being denied an opportunity to spend a fifth year in college under newly adopted NCAA rules allowing for five full years of competition. In all, the NCAA says there are approximately 450 athlete plaintiffs seeking additional eligibility through litigation, with some 300 of them winning the ability to play at least for now.

NCAA attorney Taylor Askew said the number of disputes actually strengthens the argument that the NCAA is trying to enforce rules fairly.

"That can't be arbitrary," Askew said. "It's consistency."

The athletes in the case who signed pro contracts have argued they did so only because current rules that would have allowed them another college season weren't adopted until after their decisions to sign NFL contracts.

The SEC contended the question before the judge narrowly regarded whether the conference "can enforce and require its member institutions to comply with SEC rules." The SEC's new penalties include fines up to half of a given sport's revenues, up to half-season suspensions for coaches and member universities' loss of voting privileges on league business matters.

Sankey provided an affidavit stating that SEC university presidents had voted 15-0 in favor of those penalties, with LSU's Wade Rousse abstaining.

The fight over eligibility between schools and their own conferences and the NCAA has simmered for months and spilled into politics.

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry posted on X to attorneys general in Georgia and South Carolina that "calling them 'NFL players' is at best disingenuous, and at worst intentionally deceptive."

"They are not professional football players circling back after years in the NFL," Landry wrote. "They are college players who were told, by the NCAA, that they were done. So they took the only door that was open — only to watch the NCAA change the lock behind them."

articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Atlético analizó el partido ante el Athletic y el final del mercado: "Mateu ha hecho un grandísimo trabajo".
articles.summary: El entrenador del Atlético analizó el partido ante el Athletic y el final del mercado: "Mateu ha hecho un grandísimo trabajo".
articles.body: Diego Pablo Simeone atendió a los medios antes del choque ante el Athletic de mañana. Julián sigue en el club: "Está entrenando muy bien. Va a ser convocado, esperando lo mejor de él como de todos sus compañeros" Llorente y su retirada de la selección: "Acá jugará hasta donde decida. Es una persona con las cosas muy claras, esa decisión es lo que siente. Le felicito, el ego nos hace estar en un sitio donde no... Estamos muy contentos con todo lo que nos transmite". Te ha desgastado lo de Julián: "Yo miro siempre para delante, tenemos una temporada bonita y con retos. Iremos cada partido a hacerlo lo mejor posible". Balance del mercado: "Mateu ha hecho un grandísimo trabajo, contento con las posibilidades que nos han dado para competir". Cambia el plan tener delanteros: "Siempre es diferente tener delanteros o mediapuntas que llegan al gol. Mañana esperamos que cada uno dé lo mejor de cada uno". Competir con Madrid y Barça: "No va a cambiar lo que lleva sucediendo 15 años. Madrid, Barça y los demás intentando acercarnos". Jonathan David: "Necesitamos al futbolista que estuvo en el Lille. Hablamos con él y necesitamos. Le vemos entusiasmado y con ganas, ojalá el campo que nos dé lo que él quiere y esperamos". Cómo se puede revertir lo de Julián: "Yo soy muy claro, para mí la vida está llena de oportunidades. Y Julián tiene ahora una oportunidad para ajustar sus cosas. Muchas veces nos la pasamos juzgando y hay que preocuparse de hacerlo menos y aprender más. Espero que esto le haya servido como un aprendizaje. Y que esté feliz y que como le dijo ayer Futre, al que mando un abrazo, en un lindo vídeo, que lo haga marcando goles".

articles.title: Liverpool target Yankuba Minteh can still get dream move - Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler
articles.summary: Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler says Yankuba Minteh can still "fulfil his dream" move in future after the Seagulls turned down Liverpool's offers for the winger.
articles.body:
Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler says Yankuba Minteh could still "fulfil his dream" move in the future after the club rejected Liverpool 's offers in the transfer window.

The Reds had bids of £50m and £60m turned down for the winger, with Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola having wanted to bolster his attacking options.

It is understood Brighton were seeking closer to £70m for the 22‑year‑old Gambia international.

Minteh, who joined from Newcastle for £30m in 2024, plays primarily on the right and has scored 10 goals and supplied nine assists in 73 Seagulls appearances.

Speaking before Saturday's Premier League game against Leeds , Hurzeler said: "If the whole team is successful and the individual shines then Yankuba will get a lot of attention again and he can then maybe fulfil his dream in the next transfer window."

Premier League breaks transfer record for second straight summer

Brighton reject Liverpool's new £60m Minteh bid

Hurzeler said Minteh is "definitely" committed to Brighton despite the failed move to Merseyside.

"He wears the Brighton colours, he wears the Brighton badge. He has been with us for two years now as part of the squad. He has achieved great things together with the boys," said the German.

"It's also about him now to commit. In the end, we always say we want to be successful as a club and then you can shine as individuals.

"That is what we have proved in the past. If we achieve things together, the attention will come to the individual players and that will be the case also this season."

Even though Minteh did not leave the club, Brighton still raised significant funds through player sales in the window, including Carlos Baleba's £70m move to Manchester United .

After generating those funds, Brighton completed a deadline move for Spanish defensive midfielder Chema Andres from Stuttgart in a deal worth £15.5m.

Andres made 41 appearances for Stuttgart last season after joining from Real Madrid in 2025.

He came through Real's youth set-up and made his La Liga debut in January 2025, before helping Stuttgart qualify for the Champions League in his one season at the club.

After securing the 21-year-old's signature, Hurzeler said he "understands" why the Spaniard has been dubbed 'baby Rodri'.

"He has this motivation of wanting to improve every day," said Hurzeler.

"He comes on the first day and wants to go outside on the pitch, he wants to have ball touches and you can really feel that he is very ambitious...

"Therefore, I can understand this comparison [with Rodri] but he has a long way to go and hopefully he can get there one day. It would be a big one for us but also for the whole football world."

articles.title: Julen Lobete se rompe el cruzado y será baja todo el curso
articles.standfirst: El jugador se lesionó de manera fortuita en un entrenamiento
articles.summary: El jugador se lesionó de manera fortuita en un entrenamiento
articles.body: El Málaga CF afronta un nuevo problema en su línea ofensiva. Julen Lobete se perderá lo que resta de temporada después de sufrir una importante lesión en su rodilla izquierda durante el entrenamiento de este jueves. El delantero tuvo que abandonar la sesión tras una acción fortuita y las pruebas médicas posteriores han confirmado el peor diagnóstico: rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior y lesión del ligamento colateral interno. El atacante de Lezo tendrá que pasar por el quirófano en las próximas fechas. La lesión supone un duro contratiempo para Juanfran Funes, que ve cómo se reduce todavía más el número de efectivos disponibles en ataque. Aaron Ochoa también permanece de baja tras su lesión de menisco, que igualmente requerirá intervención quirúrgica y le mantendrá alejado de los terrenos de juego durante varios meses. El infortunio de Lobete llega, además, apenas 24 horas después de que Loren Juarros respaldara públicamente su continuidad en el Málaga durante la rueda de prensa posterior al cierre del mercado. El director deportivo justificó entonces la decisión de mantener al delantero en la plantilla pese a la competencia existente en su posición. “Se queda por una decisión deportiva. De la dirección deportiva como del entrenador. Creemos que puede dar más. Entendemos que no ha dado lo que podría dar. Veremos lo que pasa porque hay mucha competencia en esa posición y además se exige mucho trabajo más en un estilo como el nuestro. En el tema de Julen, vamos a intentar que sea un jugador válido, porque puede serlo”, explicó Juarros.

articles.title: ESPN College GameDay 2026 Week 1 Schedule, Location, Predictions and More
articles.summary: ESPN College GameDay returns for the 2026 college football season, kicking off with a highly anticipated matchup between #11 LSU and Clemson.
articles.body:
ESPN College GameDay returns for the 2026 college football season, kicking off with a highly anticipated matchup between #11 LSU and Clemson.

Check below to see where and when you can catch Saturday's pregame festivities.

Location: LSU Campus in Baton Rouge, Louisiana

Crew: Rece Davis, Kirk Herbstreit, Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, Nick Saban, "Stanford Steve" Couglin, Pete Thamel, Jen Lada, and Jess Sims

The Clemson Tigers' 2025 season did not unfold as expected. Head coach Dabo Swinney has already made that abundantly clear.

A supposedly national-championship-contending team started 1-3 and never recovered. Ranked fourth in the 2025 AP Preseason Poll, the Tigers finished with six losses, their most in a season since 2010.

But Saturday starts a new season for the Tigers, unranked in the preseason poll for the first time since 2011.

However, they'll open the season in a rowdy environment at LSU.

Last season, LSU also did not meet expectations, firing head coach Brian Kelly after a 5-3 start.

But it's been a busy offseason for new head coach Lane Kiffin, looking to establish LSU as a powerhouse once again.

Kiffin has brought in the top-ranked transfer portal class per 247Sports , signing three of the top seven transfers.

Former Arizona St quarterback Sam Leavitt is set to take over for Garrett Nussmeier, who was selected by the Kansas City Chiefs in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft.

Leavitt is recovering from a foot surgery that ended his season in October.

Leavitt had a standout freshman season and was the 2024 Big 12 Offensive Freshman of the Year, leading all FBS freshmen with 11 wins as starting quarterback.

On the other end of the field, Clemson will also begin with a new quarterback—albeit a significantly less experienced one.

Cade Klubnik was drafted by the New York Jets, opening up the quarterback battle for the top spot. Former 4-star recruit Christopher Vizzina won the battle and will make his second career start.

While Clemson will look to show last season was a one-off, there's something to be said about an inexperienced quarterback opening the season in one of the toughest college football environments.

There's certainly a ton of hype on this LSU squad with the Kiffin hiring and all of the transfers they've brought in. Tomorrow, at least for one day, they'll justify that hype, beginning the season with a dominant win over Clemson.

articles.title: B/R Experts Bold Predictions for the 2026 College Football Season
articles.summary: The long, national wait is over. It's college football season, and even though we'll be at each other's throats soon enough, can the entire congregation at least say a united, "Amen!" for that?
articles.body:
The long, national wait is over. It's college football season, and even though we'll be at each other's throats soon enough, can the entire congregation at least say a united, "Amen!" for that?

So, let's get all this straight: The Big Ten rules. The SEC is looking up and saddled with a new nine-game conference schedule, too. The ACC is trying to prove it's more than just Miami, and the Big 12 is seeking national relevance, too.

Marquee quarterbacks like Dante Moore, Julian Sayin and Arch Manning rule a gaudy group of returning playmakers. But Jeremiah Smith looks like a cut above the rest of the talent.

Will all that come to fruition? CFB almost never actually "holds serve," in the expectation department now, does it? That's what bold projections are for, and that's why we're here.

Each member of our CFB writing staff—David Kenyon, Adam Kramer, Joel Reuter and Brad Shepard—made one team-specific prediction and one player-specific prediction for the season ahead.

Let's get down to the bold takes and hope they don't become cold takes.

Kenyon: Jeremiah Smith Hits 1,500 Yards in Regular Season

There is nothing bold about saying Jeremiah Smith is the best receiver in the nation.

Already a two-time AP All-American selection, he's presumably headed for a three-year sweep—before entering the 2027 NFL draft as a projected top pick. He is a superstar.

It would only be fitting for OSU's playmaker to put up special numbers in his last college season. But that's not simply a credit to his prodigious talent.

Smith will probably need to take on a heavier share of targets in 2026. He shared the position with Emeka Egbuka and Carnell Tate in 2024, then Tate again in 2025. Ohio State is never thin on depth at receiver, but it seems unlikely Brandon Inniss or true freshman Chris Henry Jr. will be 1,000-yard players this year.

Not only is Smith capable of filling that production void, but the difficulty of OSU's schedule may actually help, too. Since the Buckeyes wrecked everyone en route to 12-0 last year, Smith tallied just 10 catches in the fourth quarter. More competitive games in 2026 should lead to more receptions, as well.

Smith has a great shot to become only the second wideout in a half-decade to hit 1,500 yards during the regular season.

Kramer: Keelon Russell Will Be a Superstar by Halloween

Have you seen his highlights? Sure, it was high school. I get that. It was also a few years ago.

But Alabama's new starting quarterback has truly rare traits, and the former 5-star recruit blessed with size, speed and a remarkable arm won't need long to make an impact on the SEC and college football as a whole.

Alabama was right to take it slow with him last year. Russell saw time against Louisiana Monroe and Eastern Illinois, looking plenty competent in both instances. But a year spent learning and growing should pay enormous dividends, and it will pay dividends early on.

The schedule is conducive for a fast start. A road game at Kentucky in Week 2 could offer up some resistance, although the first five games come against manageable opponents. In October, Russell will play Georgia, Tennessee and LSU. This is where it will come together.

It won't always be perfect, but it will be electric. Get ready to meet CFB's newest superstar.

Reuter: Devon Dampier is a Heisman Trophy Finalist

After racking up 2,768 passing yards, 1,166 rushing yards and 31 total touchdowns at New Mexico during the 2024 season, quarterback Devon Dampier transferred to Utah last season and helped lead the Utes to an 11-2 record.

Despite the step up in competition playing the Big 12, he took a significant step forward with his completion percentage (57.9 percent to 63.5 percent), interception rate (3.1 percent to 1.5 percent) and passer rating (121.6 to 146.8) while continuing to be a dual-threat contributor with 2,490 passing yards, 835 rushing yards and 34 touchdowns.

He did all of that while playing through a sports hernia that required offseason surgery and also navigating ankle and leg injuries.

With a clean bill of health, another step forward is not out of the question, and that could make the Utes Big 12 contenders and earn him a seat in New York.

Shepard: LaNorris Sellers Rebounds to Become a Top-10 Draft Pick

If Shane Beamer doesn't turn things around at South Carolina after an abysmal 4-8 season that saw his Gamecocks win just one SEC game, he's toast.

It may be an uphill battle for them to post a winning season this year, but they are a sneaky-solid pick to rebound if redshirt junior LaNorris Sellers can regain his old form.

A season ago, Sellers looked lost in Mike Shula's offense, completing just 61 percent of his passes for 2,437 yards, 13 touchdowns and eight interceptions and running for just 270 yards after 674 in '24. All this for a guy who was a trendy pick to be the top overall player taken in this year's NFL draft.

Shula was relieved of his duties in November, and Sellers' play improved down the stretch. This offseason, Beamer hired veteran offensive coordinator Kendal Briles from TCU to help Sellers regain his old dual-threat form.

He's going to put up the kind of numbers that calm NFL executives' fears, and that 6'3", 238-pound frame will help push him back up draft boards.

Heading into the 2026 campaign, the ACC is all about Miami. After finishing as the national runner-up, the 'Canes reloaded with a few flashy transfers to complement a strong core of returning players. They should be excellent this year.

Back in 2023, the Mustangs exited the American with an 11-3 mark and a conference title. They debuted as part of the ACC in 2024, rattling off another 11-win record that included an appearance in the College Football Playoff. SMU squandered a chance to make the ACC Championship Game with a loss in 2025's regular-season finale but still posted a 9-4 record. This program is a consistent threat.

Led by veteran QB Kevin Jennings, SMU should be a contender yet again. There are trips to Florida State, Louisville and Notre Dame on the docket, but that's not exactly a gauntlet. Miami, Clemson and Pitt aren't on the slate, and the Mustangs get Virginia and Virginia Tech at home. The schedule is plenty favorable.

Even if Miami, for example, were to beat SMU in the ACC title game, an 11-2 record may be enough for the Mustangs to snatch one of the CFP's last at-large bids.

Kramer: Oregon Will Break Through and Win the National Championship

Oh, the Ducks have been close. Under Chip Kelly, they were a few flipped plays away from a national championship. Under Dan Lanning, there has been a mix of close calls and remarkable progress.

This roster is the best he's ever had. It's also the most balanced group in all of college football.

Quarterback Dante Moore said no to the Jets to get at least one more crack at winning a title, and he's surrounded by playmakers in his second year with the Ducks. Defensively, Oregon has one of the strongest defensive lines in all of college football coupled with a slew of playmakers on the back end.

This team is good—really, really good. And although the schedule features tricky road games at USC and Ohio State, it will only help this team come playoff time.

Oregon has flirted with a natty in recent years. This year, it all finally comes together.

Reuter: Oklahoma Wins a College Football Playoff Game

The Sooners open the season at No. 10 in the AP poll, putting them squarely on the College Football Playoff bubble, but they are capable of shaking up the playoff bracket.

Defense has been a strength under head coach Brent Venables, and they ranked in the top 10 in the nation last year in yards allowed (272.5, sixth) and points allowed (15.5, seventh). With six returning starters, expect it to be a major strength once again.

The X-factor will be the health and production of quarterback John Mateer. He was a legitimate Heisman Trophy candidate last season before suffering a broken bone in his throwing hand. He wasn't the same threat in the passing game when he returned, but a healthy Mateer should again be one of the nation's most dynamic dual-threat quarterbacks.

Their schedule is daunting, with Michigan, Georgia and Texas early before they close out the year with Ole Miss, Texas A&M and Missouri in a three-week span. If they can survive, they'll be as battle-tested as any team in the country.

Shepard: North Dakota State Will Play in College Football Playoff in Its Inaugural FBS Season

For years, North Dakota State was even more dominant in the Football Championship Subdivision than Nick Saban-led Alabama.

Finally, the bullies are picking on somebody their own size.

News flash: If Week 0 is any indication, the Bison are still bullies.

They whipped Jacksonville State 33-7 in the Fargo Dome last weekend in their first-ever game on this level. The Gamecocks aren't some slouch, either. They were in the Conference USA title game last year and picked third again.

NDSU obliterated them, using the same defense-first formula that kept them dominant in the lower level for years. Coach Tim Polacek isn't fixing something that's not broken.

With the triumvirate of AAC coaches (Jon Sumrall to Florida, Alex Golesh to Auburn and Ryan Silverfield to Arkansas) off to the SEC, that league could suffer. That leaves the Group of Six CFP berth wide-open.

Boise State and Fresno State will be tough in the new-look Pac-12, but NDSU might just be the beast in the Mountain West, especially after UNLV looked susceptible last week.

The bold guess is the Bison's success translates.

articles.title: Bernat: "Entrenar con Messi es una barbaridad; no creo que vayamos a ver a otro como él"
articles.standfirst: El valenciano, tras pasar varias veces por quirófano, busca en el Eibar recuperar su mejor nivel tras una carrera brillante en Bayern y PSG
articles.summary: El valenciano, tras pasar varias veces por quirófano, busca en el Eibar recuperar su mejor nivel tras una carrera brillante en Bayern y PSG
articles.body: Por la banda izquierda de Ipurua asoman 18 títulos desde que en el mes de febrero Juan Bernat (Cullera, 1993) acudiera a la llamada de César Palacios para fichar por el Eibar. Tras pasar dos veces por el quirófano por una pubalgia, el lateral se refugiaba en el ambiente familiar armero para volver disfrutar de su pasión por el fútbol. Ha compartido vestuario con jugadores como Mbappé, Messi, Neymar, Ribéry o Robben, pero no se le caen los anillos por jugar en un club humilde como el Eibar, donde encajó de maravilla desde el primer día y ahora busca recuperar su mejor nivel. Cree que hay plantilla para soñar con cosas grandes y no renuncia a nada. Después de un par de temporadas en las que las lesiones le han impedido tener continuidad, por fin ha podido tener una pretemporada en condiciones. ¿Cómo se encuentra? Mi primer objetivo era poder hacer una pretemporada completa. En año y medio he tenido dos operaciones de pubalgia que no me han dejado tener continuidad. Quería empezar entrenando desde el principio para poder llegar en las mejores condiciones al inicio liguero y creo que voy por buen camino. ¿Cómo fueron esos meses entrenando en solitario para recuperarse de la lesión? ¿Se le pasó por la cabeza dejar el fútbol en algún momento? Difíciles. Quería jugar al fútbol en España y mi situación era complicada. Tenía claro que no lo iba a dejar, pero tampoco me apetecía salir al extranjero. Con 32 años me veía bien. Es verdad que había tenido mala suerte con las dos lesiones, sabía que tenía que trabajar mucho y mantenerme bien físicamente para aprovechar la oportunidad cuando me llegara, aunque el ritmo te lo da la competición y por muy fuerte que entrenes en solitario, no estás igual los compañeros. En esos momentos uno ve quiénes están de verdad ahí. Siempre he tenido claro cuál es mi círculo cercano que son la familia y los amigos. Cuando juegas en grandes equipos siempre se te acerca gente, pero tengo buen ojo para detectar eso y no he tenido ningún problema. Estuve en Valencia durante todo ese tiempo y disfrutando de otro aspecto de la vida que no había tenido durante muchos años. El fútbol encima es cruel porque cuando sales de la rueda luego no es fácil volver. La gente se olvida cuando estás fuera un tiempo. Ocho meses sin competir ya era mucho tiempo y no quería estar más tiempo. Quería volver a engancharme y coger ritmo para poder acabar la temporada. Cuando llegué al Eibar tuve mala suerte porque después de mi debut me hice daño en el tobillo. Volví a las dos semanas, pero no estaba bien y tuve que parar otra vez. Sólo pude jugar dos partidos de inicio y tampoco cogí mucho ritmo. Ha sido titular en las tres primeras jornadas a un buen nivel. ¿Cuánto le queda para llegar a tu mejor versión? Me he encontrado bien en estos dos primeros partidos. Cada día estoy mejor, con más ritmo y fuerza en las piernas. Creo que estoy cerca de llegar al 100% y ojalá pueda seguir disfrutando del fútbol que al final es lo que quiero. Ha estado muchos años en el extranjero y priorizó seguir en el fútbol español. ¿Por qué eligió el Eibar? La última operación de pubalgia coincidió con el final de la temporada. Estuve todo el verano recuperándome y la verdad es que después de todo eso, tampoco tenía muchas opciones en España. Cuando salió la posibilidad de venir al Eibar, no me lo pensé dos veces. Hay muchos jugadores que cuando lo han ganado todo, como es su caso, deciden irse lejos para ganar mucho dinero. En su caso ha sido al revés. En muchos sitios podría tener un sueldo mucho más alto del que tiene en el Eibar. Conseguí muchos títulos en el extranjero, que era uno de mis objetivos. No es fácil ganar títulos porque son pocos los equipos que lo hacen y en ese aspecto lo cumplí. Había estado nueve años fuera de España y tenía la espinita de disfrutar del fútbol en mi país. El dinero no era algo que me importara porque lo que quería era estar aquí. ¿Cómo cambia el chip un futbolista de jugar partidos de Champions en grandes escenarios a hacerlo en una categoría como Segunda? Con humildad. A mí lo que me gusta es jugar al fútbol y competir. Es verdad que he jugado en grandes equipos y en competiciones europeas, pero ahora estoy disfrutando mucho aquí. Venir a entrenar todos los días es un placer y ojalá podamos conseguir grandes cosas esta temporada. Creo que tenemos un grupo muy bueno. ¿Cambiaría alguno de sus 18 títulos por subir a Primera con el Eibar? Sin duda. Por subir a Primera con el Eibar, cambiaba alguno seguro. Ha pasado de convivir en un vestuario como el del Bayern o el PSG a hacerlo en el del Eibar. Las diferencias tienen que ser considerables, ¿no? Allí hay jugadores muy reconocidos mundialmente y no siempre es fácil manejar los egos. Además, en esos equipos hay muchas nacionalidades dentro del vestuario y a veces por el tema de los idiomas no nos entendemos todos igual. Aquí todos hablamos castellano, nos llevamos muy bien entre todos y el ambiente es increíble. ¿Qué destacaría del Eibar? Somos una cuadrilla de amigos. Todos nos llevamos bien. Disfrutamos entrenando y compitiendo. El día que me vaya del Eibar me llevaré grandes amigos y grandes personas. Es un placer compartir el día a día con los compañeros, con los trabajadores, con el director deportivo y con la presidenta. El Eibar es un club muy top en ese aspecto. ¿Uno llega a valorar los títulos ligueros en clubes como Bayern y PSG en los que todo el mundo les da por campeones desde la primera jornada? Sí se valora. Los futbolistas competimos para ganar títulos. Es verdad que con Bayern y PSG éramos muy favoritos y dominábamos la mayoría de los partidos, pero claro que los disfrutas. En el fútbol va todo muy deprisa y cuando me retire, podré decir que he hecho una gran carrera. A mí me gusta jugar al fútbol más allá del equipo en el que esté y creo que hoy se está perdiendo esa esencia. A la gente joven cada vez le gusta menos. Es verdad que el fútbol es cada vez más físico. Hace 15 años veías a muchos niños jugando en la calle al fútbol. Ahora hay muchas más distracciones que tampoco ayudan y eso es lo que echo de menos. Con el palmarés llama la atención sus pocas internacionalidades. ¿Cree que al jugador español se le valora menos cuando está fuera? Puede que cuando estás fuera de España no tengas tanto alcance, pero estoy orgulloso de mis once internacionalidades. ¿Qué podría haber ido más veces convocado? Igual sí. Pero representar a tu país es una de las cosas más bonitas. En la Selección hay un nivel muy alto, mucha competencia en todos los puestos y es difícil entrar en una convocatoria. A su edad y con todo el recorrido que tiene, ¿aún se pone nervioso antes de un partido? Siempre tienes el gusanillo antes del partido de querer ganar y hacerlo bien. Obviamente, la presión no es la misma, pero esos nervios el día antes siempre están ahí. El día que desaparezca todo eso, será el momento de dejarlo. Son muchos los niños que sueñan con ser futbolistas, pero muy pocos llegan a serlo. ¿En qué momento sintió que podía vivir del fútbol? Desde que tenía 6 años soñaba con ser futbolista y he hecho todo lo posible para lograrlo, aunque luego siempre hay variantes que pueden impedírtelo. En mi cabeza tenía claro que iba a lograrlo, aunque no es fácil porque muchos niños quieren ser futbolistas y la mayoría no lo consiguen. Ha habido un esfuerzo detrás y siempre he sido muy disciplinado. Cuando tienes pasión por algo y haces todo lo posible por lograrlo, lo puedes conseguir. El talento lo traía de serie, pero ¿cuánto de importante fueron sus padres en ese recorrido por las categorías inferiores del Valencia? Mucho. Desde los 6 años hasta los 18 eran los que me llevaban a los entrenamientos y a los partidos. He sido muy afortunado de tener los padres que tengo y en parte soy futbolista gracias a ellos. Son los mejores padres del mundo. Pasó de debutar con el Valencia a en cuestión de dos años estar en un vestuario como el del Bayern. Todo fue muy rápido. ¿En algún momento tuvieron que bajarle de la nube? No hizo falta por la forma en la que me habían educado. Siempre he estado muy unido a ellos y he tenido las cosas claras. No he tenido ningún momento malo en ese sentido. Tampoco me agobiaban mucho con el tema del fútbol. Hoy en día se ven algunos padres que tienen más ganas que sus hijos de ser futbolista. En ese aspecto tuve suerte. Ellos sabían que me gustaba el fútbol, me dejaban disfrutar y si algún día me tenían que decir que lo había hecho mal, lo hacían. ¿Trabajar con Guardiola cambió su manera de entender el juego? Había visto mucho al Barcelona de Pep porque a mí es el fútbol que más me gusta. Intentar ser superior al rival a través del control del balón. El día a día con él en Munich era un privilegio. Para mí es el mejor entrenador de la historia. Aprender y entrenar con él fue un placer. ¿Se ve como entrenador en un futuro? Hasta hace unos años no me veía, pero ahora que se acerca el final, aunque espero que aún me queden unas temporadas, estoy cambiando de idea. Puede que me pique el gusanillo. Intentaré sacarme el título y probaré. Si veo que no me termina de convencer lo dejaré porque me gusta hacer las cosas si sientes pasión por ellas. Messi, Mbappé, Neymar, Robben, Ribéry, Neuer... Pocos jugadores pueden presumir de haber compartido vestuario con tantas estrellas como usted. ¿Le falta alguno? Cristiano es el que me falta, pero puedo estar más que satisfecho de haber entrenado a diario con todos esos jugadores. ¿Cómo es compartir banda con Mbappé o Neymar? Cuando les doblas, muchas veces sabes que no te van a dar el balón, pero lo haces para quitarles algún rival de encima y para que así ellos tengan más posibilidades de ver portería. Son jugadores que tienen un uno contra uno bestial y no es que no te la den porque no quieran, sino porque es lo mejor para el equipo. No se caracterizan por defender mucho, pero entre los mediocentros y los defensas equilibramos un poco eso. Los que han jugado con Messi dicen que lo que hace en los entrenamientos es más impactante que lo que hace en los partidos. En los entrenamientos siempre hay partidos más reducidos, entra más veces en contacto con el balón y ahí se ven más acciones repetidas. Es una barbaridad. Es el mejor jugador de la historia y no creo que vayamos a ver otro como él. Cuando está dentro del campo con tipos de ese nivel, ¿llega a disfrutar como un espectador de lo que hacen? Sí, disfrutas y además te lo pasas bien jugando con ellos porque entienden el fútbol, aguantan la pelota en situaciones complicados y tienen capacidad para decidir los partidos. ¿A su edad uno piensa más en seguir creciendo a todos los niveles o en mantener su estado de un año a otro? Siempre intentas mejorar, pero por edad vamos a ir hacia abajo. Hoy en día se miden todos los datos físicos y si no eres capaz de mantener eso, no te va a dar para competir porque el fútbol ha evolucionado mucho y hay que estar muy preparado. Tenemos muchos más recursos para cuidarnos. Somos atletas y el objetivo es tener continuidad y jugar todo lo que se pueda. ¿Se cuida mucho fuera del campo? Siempre me ha gustado mucho cuidarme y entrenar. Le dedico muchas horas al gimnasio. La genética también me ayuda y es agradecida conmigo. Al final vivo de mi cuerpo y trato de cuidarme todo lo que puedo.

articles.summary: Title holders Barcelona will face last season's semi-finalists Bayern Munich and Arsenal in the league phase of the women's Champions League. Barça defeated...
articles.body:
Title holders Barcelona will face last season's semi-finalists Bayern Munich and Arsenal in the league phase of the women's Champions League.

Barça defeated Bayern in the semi-finals last term, while Arsenal lost to Lyon. The Spanish team went on to beat Lyon 4-0 in the final.

The title holders will also face Paris FC, Roma, Servette and HB Køge.

Friday's draw also pitched Lyon and Arsenal against each other again in the first phase of the tournament.

Besides Barcelona, Bayern will face, among others, Paris Saint-Germain, Manchester City and Real Madrid.

The women's Champions League starts on September 22.

articles.title: Una liguilla con morbo
articles.standfirst: El Barcelona recibirá al Arsenal de Mariona, Ona y Misa; y el Real Madrid al Inter de Ivana y Sheila
articles.summary: Ambos reciben a Paris FC en casa y visitan los feudos de Bayern y Roma
articles.body: La sede de la UEFA en Nyon ha sido el escenario elegido para el sorteo de la fase Liga de la Women's Champions League que ha definido el inicio del camino de Barcelona y Real Madrid hasta la meta que este año estará ubicada en Varsovia. Las azulgrana se han visto emparejadas con Arsenal, Paris FC, Servette -en casa-, Bayern, Roma y HB Køge -fuera-; mientras que las blancas se medirán a PSG, Paris FC e Inter -en casa-, Bayern, Roma y Manchester City -fuera- en esta ronda. El Barcelona buscará la defensa de su título y la quinta corona continental. El conjunto dirigido por Pere Romeu ya sabe lo que es jugar ante cinco de los seis rivales que tendrá en su puesta en escena en la liguilla. En casa recibirá al Arsenal, con quien se ha enfrentado en cinco ocasiones (dos victorias y tres derrotas) y donde el morbo lo pone medirse al verdugo en la final de Lisboa en 2025 y el reencuentro con Mariona Caldentey y Ona Batlle, amén de Misa Rodríguez; al Paris FC, a quien ha ganado en el único precedente entre ambos; y al Servette, el único de sus rivales con el que no tiene historia. Por su parte, jugará a domicilio frente al Bayern, con quien ha jugado hasta en siete ocasiones (cinco victorias, un empate y una derrota); Roma, a quien ha ganado en sus tres duelos previos; y HB Køge, a quien ha vencido en los dos precedentes disputados. El Real Madrid tiene como objetivo superar la barrera de cuartos de final en la máxima competición europea y, por qué no, aspirar a más. El equipo dirigido por Pau Quesada se medirá en esta fase Liga a viejos conocidos. En casa jugarán ante PSG, equipo ante el que se ha medido en cuatro ocasiones (un empate y tres derrotas); Paris FC, ante quien ha perdido en los dos partidos disputados hasta la fecha; e Inter, que será el primer rival italiano ante el que se enfrente y contará con el morbo de ver enfrente a dos ex como Ivana Andrés y Sheila García. Por su parte, las blancas tendrán que viajar fuera para medirse al Manchester City, rival al que se han enfrentado en tres ocasiones (dos victorias y un empate); así como Bayern y Roma, ante los que no existe historial. La fase Liga de la Champions League se disputará en seis jornadas, jugando cada equipo tres partidos como local y tres como visitantes en las siguientes fechas: 22 y 23 de septiembre; 30 de septiembre y 1 de octubre; 28 y 29 de octubre; 10 y 11 de noviembre; 18 y 19 de noviembre y 16 de diciembre. Una vez finalizada esta fase, el 18 de diciembre se sorteará la fase de eliminatorias. Los octavos de final se jugarán a ida y vuelta los días 3 y 4 y 10 y 11 de febrero; los cuartos de final los días 22 y 24 de marzo y 21 de marzo y 1 de abril; las semifinales los días 1 y 2 y 8 y 9 de mayo; y la final el 28, 29 o 30 de mayo -fecha aún sin decidir- en el Stadion Narodowy de Polonia.

articles.summary: Flick aún no ha decidido si lo citará contra el Valencia
articles.body: El Barcelona se ejercitó esta mañana en las instalaciones de la Ciudad Deportiva. En el entrenamiento de hoy, Gabriel Jesus y Gavi trabajaron al mismo ritmo que sus compañeros, después que ayer jueves se sumaran a una parte. El atacante brasileño ya ha comenzado, por lo tanto, la cuenta atrás para su debut con el Barça. Gabriel Jesus fue uno más en el entrenamiento de este viernes, el segundo que realiza junto a sus nuevos compañeros. El exjugador del Arsenal, último fichaje culé de este mercado de verano, asumió bien las cargas de trabajo, por lo que su estreno con la camiseta azulgrana está cerca. No está claro, no obstante, cuándo formará parte de la expedición. Flick todavía no ha decidido si lo convocará mañana para el encuentro contra el Valencia. Si lo hace, no sería tanto para que tenga minutos en Mestalla sino para que vaya conociendo al equipo y favorecer su adaptación al vestuario. Por otro lado, Gavi también completó toda la sesión hoy. Atrás ya ha quedado la contusión que sufrió en Elche y que le impidió estar a disposición de Flick en los compromisos contra el Athletic y el Rayo. El centrocampista andaluz estará ya citado para el partido del domingo contra el Valencia. Será alta. Así mismo, en el entrenamiento de esta mañana, igual que en el de ayer, también estuvo el joven Iu Martínez, extremo de 17 años del Juvenil A.

articles.title: Everything Deion Sanders Said About Julian Lewis, Colorado's Upset Win vs. GT in CFB Opener
articles.summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders expressed pride in quarterback Julian Lewis following a tumultuous season opener his team won after a late touchdown drive and a blocked field goal.
articles.body:
Colorado coach Deion Sanders expressed pride in quarterback Julian Lewis following a tumultuous season opener his team won after a late touchdown drive and a blocked field goal.

Sanders told reporters after Colorado's 14-13 season-opening win he was glad Lewis completed the clutch scoring drive "because you guys would have been eating him alive if he hadn't."

"The kid is still young. He's still growing... I want you guys to give him time," Sanders said Thursday night.

First look at Pro Bowler coaching for CFB team

The Buffaloes offense got the ball for the last time Thursday night with just over one minute left on the clock.

"I said, 'Look, I'm getting ready to use every one of these timeouts," Sanders said. "'You're probably gonna have a minute-something left on the clock. Go to work, because we're not going to have a timeout, so they're not going to be up because they don't want to get beat deep. They don't want to do that. We're going to have a chance to catch and get out of bounds.'

"And he dialed it up. He dialed the correct play, and JuJu made the throw. I'm proud of him."

Lewis, a redshirt freshman, appeared in four games for the Buffaloes last season before winning the starting job this summer.

articles.title: Noel Gallagher sobre Enzo: "Ha pedido el dorsal de De Bruyne, eso demuestra que tiene huevos"
articles.standfirst: El cantante británico, fan acérrimo del Manchester City, está encantado con el fichaje de Enzo Fernández por su club: "Es el jugador que necesitábamos"
articles.summary: El cantante británico, fan acérrimo del Manchester City, está encantado con el fichaje de Enzo Fernández por su club: "Es el jugador que necesitábamos"
articles.body: La llegada de Enzo al Manchester City ha despertado una enorme expectación entre los aficionados celestes, y Noel Gallagher no ha tardado en mostrar su entusiasmo. El emblemático cantante de Oasis, reconocido seguidor del City, aseguró que el argentino reúne las características que el equipo venía buscando para reforzar su centro del campo. "Enzo es exactamente el jugador que necesitamos", afirmó sin rodeos en Talksport. Gallagher destacó especialmente el carácter competitivo del mediocampista, un perfil que considera fundamental para elevar el nivel de exigencia del equipo. "Nos ha faltado eso", explicó el músico, antes de profundizar en una comparación tan llamativa como significativa. "Queríamos un jugador similar a Roy Keane, no por ponerlo a su nivel, pero que se le plante a los rivales", señaló, dejando claro que valora la personalidad del argentino por encima de cualquier otra cualidad. Para el cantante británico, la incorporación de Enzo aporta un componente de intensidad que no encuentra en otros futbolistas de la plantilla. "Quiero eso en el City, porque Phil (Foden) no va a hacerlo, Elliott Anderson no va a hacerlo", reflexionó Gallagher, convencido de que el nuevo fichaje puede convertirse en el futbolista encargado de imponer respeto en la batalla del mediocampo. Más allá de su rendimiento dentro del terreno de juego, Gallagher también se mostró cautivado por la actitud del internacional argentino desde su llegada al club. "Me pone contento que esté aquí", confesó, antes de revelar un detalle que le llamó especialmente la atención y que interpreta como una declaración de intenciones del jugador. El artista destacó la elección del dorsal que había dejado libre Kevin De Bruyne, un gesto que, a su juicio, demuestra una personalidad fuerte y una mentalidad ambiciosa. "Me gustó que pida la camiseta de Kevin, porque te garantizo que no se la iban a ofrecer", aseguró entre risas. Y remató con una frase que resume perfectamente su admiración por el argentino: "Eso demuestra que tiene huevos. Me encanta".

articles.title: Women's Champions League 2026/27 draw: Arsenal to face reigning champions Barcelona, Chelsea and Man City to play PSG
articles.summary: Last season's semi-finalists Arsenal will play reigning champions Barcelona in the Women's Champions League league phase; Chelsea to face Paris Saint-Germain; Man City ; league phase matches take place between September 22 and December 16
articles.body:
The Gunners - semi-finalists last season - will also face OL Lyonnes, Benfica, Paris FC, HB Koge and Inter Milan across six matchdays between September 22 and December 16.

Chelsea have been drawn against Paris Saint-Germain, OL Lyonnes, Roma, BK Hacken, Austria Wien and OH Leuven.

Meanwhile, WSL champions Man City - taking part in the competition for the first time since 2024/25 - will also play Paris Saint-Germain, Inter Milan, BK Hacken and Austria Wien, as well as Bayern Munich and Real Madrid.

Arsenal : OL Lyonnes (H), Barcelona (A), Benfica (H), Paris FC (A), HB Koge (H) Inter Milan (A)

Chelsea : Paris Saint-Germain (H), OL Lyonnes (A), Roma (H), BK Hacken (A), Austria Wien (H), OH Leuven (A)

Man City : Paris Saint-Germain (H), Bayern Munich (A), Real Madrid (H), BK Hacken (A), Austria Wien (H), Inter Milan (A)

What are the Champions League key dates?

May 28/29 or 30 - Stadion Narodowy, Warsaw
